baardman.name: Baardman (belman)
baardman.season_note: A resident fish. ORI and De Hoop tagging show very little movement along the coast, and the fish stay close to home caves (Mann 2013), so they are present all year. Cape shore reports cluster in late autumn and winter, roughly May to September, on the northern False Bay beaches: Broken Road and Macassar in late May 2025, Strandfontein, Mnandi, Macassar and Strand as 'prime time' in June 2025, Strand in July 2025, and Swartklip in May 2007. Winter 2022 was 'an extremely poor year for belman' at Strand and Macassar. Summer catches are not reported, probably because the south-easter makes these south-facing beaches rough. Western Cape fish spawn November to February (Mann 2013). The species ranges from Cape Point eastward, so Atlantic-side 'belman' reports are doubtful. The shore between the Eerste River mouth (Macassar) and the Lourens River mouth (Strand) is the Helderberg MPA, which is closed to fishing: fish Macassar west of the Eerste mouth and the Strand east of the Lourens mouth.

temp.basis: estimate. The range runs from Cape Point to Oman (Mann 2013), so it tolerates warm water but is absent from the cold Atlantic coast. Cape catches peak in winter, when northern False Bay surf is about 14 to 16 C. No thermal study found.

baardman.habitat: Adults use sandy substrata, mixed rock-and-sand surf zones and subtidal reef, and are most often associated with high-relief limestone or sandstone reef (Mann 2013). By day adults gather in reef caves and return to the same 'home' caves (Mann 2013, from diver counts). Shore anglers fish sand banks and the gutters of mixed rock-and-sand ground beside that reef. On the page's spots this means the reef-and-sand stretches from Swartklip and Strandfontein through Mnandi and Monwabisi to Macassar (west of the Eerste River mouth) and the Strand (east of the Lourens River mouth). The coast between those two river mouths is the Helderberg MPA and is closed to fishing. The Horses off Baden Powell Drive has similar ground, but no source puts belman there (inference only).
baardman.diet: Bottom invertebrates of reef and sand. Adults take polychaete worms, crustaceans (crabs, prawns) and molluscs. Juveniles eat mainly polychaetes and small crustaceans such as mysids (Mann 2013).
baardman.typical_size: Shore fish are typically 40 to 55 cm, about 0.8 to 2.2 kg on the False Bay length-weight relation (Mann 2013), and many False Bay fish are under the 40 cm limit. A 70 cm fish is about 4.5 kg. The heaviest fish sampled in False Bay weighed 8.5 kg and the longest was 80.5 cm TL (Hutchings 2005, in Mann 2013). The maximum recorded length is 87 cm TL (Kenton-on-Sea, 1989), and the record weight is 12.6 kg (spearfishing, 1956) (Mann 2013).
baardman.handling: No-sale recreational species. The bag limit is 5 per person per day and the minimum size 40 cm TL, with no closed season (Mann 2013; DFFE recreational regulations brochure, Table 4). The stock was assessed as collapsed, at under 25% of spawner biomass per recruit (about 21% in False Bay; Hutchings and Griffiths 2010, in Mann 2013). WWF-SASSI lists it as red (don't buy) and it is Near Threatened (NBA 2018). Because it is highly resident, a stretch of beach can easily be fished out. Release every undersize fish and consider releasing all of them; scientists have recommended a limit of 2 per day at 50 cm (Mann 2013). Use circle or small baitholder hooks to avoid deep hooking. Handle with wet hands, support the belly, mind the spiny dorsal fin, and release it into the backwash quickly. Never fish the shore between the Eerste and Lourens river mouths (Helderberg MPA). Safety on Swartklip, Strandfontein, Mnandi, Monwabisi and Macassar: go in a group at all times and leave before the sun starts setting. Local anglers say these beaches should only be visited in groups and fished during the day (Sealine). Do not fish them after dark.

tactics.title: Worm bait in the second-breaker gutter
tactics.lure_or_bait: Bloodworm, wonderworm or moonshine worm (a 5 to 8 cm piece), or prawn or black/white mussel; a worm and prawn cocktail for extra scent
tactics.rig: Running sinker on a light 9 to 10 ft rod: 2 to 3 oz (56 to 85 g) star or grapnel sinker on a slider, 50 to 60 cm trace of 0.35 to 0.40 mm nylon or fluorocarbon, single 1/0 to 2/0 baitholder or circle hook
tactics.retrieve: Cast to the sand gutter just behind the second or third breaker and leave it static, lifting to resettle every few minutes. When the belman bites, drop the rod tip and give a little slack before you lift into it.
tactics.depth: On the bottom, 1 to 3 m of water in sand gutters beside reef
tactics.stand: On the beach opposite a darker gutter or rip where white water spills off the reef into sand. On the Swartklip to Macassar stretch, go in a group and fish in daylight only.
tactics.why: Jacita reports have the fish feeding close in behind the second or third breaker and give the slack-line advice. District Mail names worm, prawn and mussel as baits, on light to medium tackle with scaled-down hooks and leaders. Mann 2013 puts adults on mixed rock-and-sand surf zones beside reef, feeding on worms and crustaceans.

tactics.title: Top of the tide at first light or before sunset
tactics.lure_or_bait: Fresh worm (bloodworm, wonderworm or moonshine worm) or prawn
tactics.rig: 2 to 3 oz sliding star sinker, 50 cm 0.35 mm trace, 1/0 circle or baitholder hook
tactics.retrieve: Get the bait out an hour before high and keep it static in the gutter. Re-bait often, because worm washes out. Give slack on the bite, then lift.
tactics.depth: On the bottom in the gutter and on the sand edge of the reef
tactics.stand: In a group, on the beach in front of the deepest gutter. As the tide pushes, move back up the beach and keep fishing the same gutter. On Swartklip, Strandfontein, Mnandi, Monwabisi and Macassar, arrive once it is light and pack up before the sun starts setting, so an evening high tide is fished in the last daylight hour, not into the dark.
tactics.why: Jacita calls high tide about two hours before dawn and dusk the 'prime strike windows' for the False Bay surf, where belman were being caught. Fish that shelter in caves by day (Mann 2013) are likely to forage over sand in low light (inference). Local posts warn against staying on these beaches once the sun starts setting.
sources: Mann BQ (ed.) 2013, ORI Special Publication 9, Umbrina robinsoni profile

tactics.title: Churned water after the northerlies
tactics.lure_or_bait: Large scented worm bait (whole wonderworm or bloodworm) or worm and prawn cocktail
tactics.rig: 3 oz (85 g) grapnel sinker to hold in the churn, which is the top end of light tackle, 40 to 50 cm 0.40 mm trace, 2/0 baitholder hook
tactics.retrieve: Static. Fish the newly opened gullies close in, often just behind the second breaker, and check the bait every 10 minutes.
tactics.depth: On the bottom in freshly scoured gullies
tactics.stand: Opposite gullies opened by the wind, where foam and churned sand show bait being flushed out. Stay outside the Helderberg MPA (between the Eerste and Lourens river mouths).
tactics.why: Jacita reports northerly winds churning up the inshore seabed, opening gullies and flushing out bait, in the week of good belman catches at Broken Road and Macassar. Scent baits help in coloured water.

tactics.title: Calm clear day: scale right down
tactics.lure_or_bait: Small natural bait: a 4 to 5 cm piece of moonshine worm or a peeled prawn
tactics.rig: 1.5 to 2 oz sinker, long 1 m trace of 0.30 mm fluorocarbon, No. 1 to 1/0 hook
tactics.retrieve: Cast to the sand edge right beside the reef and leave it still; small slow lifts only
tactics.depth: On the bottom, 1.5 to 3 m, tight to the reef edge
tactics.stand: Beside the reef on the sand-and-reef sections of the beach, casting along the reef edge rather than straight out
tactics.why: District Mail recommends light to medium tackle with scaled-down hooks and leaders for belman. Jacita says 'flat surf is the name of the game' (0.8 to 1.2 m) and expected belman at Strand when the wind and swell eased, on moonshine worm.

tactics.title: Winter belman run on the northern False Bay beaches
tactics.lure_or_bait: Moonshine worm or wonderworm; prawn as backup
tactics.rig: 2 to 3 oz star sinker, 50 to 60 cm 0.35 mm trace, 1/0 hook
tactics.retrieve: Static in the gutter; give slack on the bite
tactics.depth: On the bottom, behind the second breaker
tactics.stand: In front of a gutter on the sand-and-reef stretches of the northern False Bay beaches: Strandfontein, Mnandi, Swartklip, Monwabisi, Macassar west of the Eerste River mouth, and the Strand east of the Lourens River mouth. The shore between those two mouths is the Helderberg MPA, closed to fishing. Go in a group and leave before the sun starts setting.
tactics.why: Winter reports name Strandfontein, Mnandi, Macassar and the Strand as 'prime time for targeting Baardman' (June 2025), Broken Road and Macassar (May 2025), and the Strand on moonshine worm (July 2025). Strand and Macassar are called 'belman hot spots' (District Mail, Sept 2022), and belman were caught at Swartklip on prawn and wonderworm (May 2007). Local posts say this stretch should be fished in groups and in daylight.

legal.bag_note: 5 per day. Counts toward the aggregate of 10.
legal.note: A and B agree and both match R.959. No closed season. 'Belman', 'bellman' and 'baardman' are the same fish.
legal.quote: Baardman (bellman, tasselfish) | Umbrina spp. | 40 cm | 5

baardman.review: Checked by an independent skeptic; 15 corrections applied
review_points: Mann 2013 says the opposite about relief: adults are 'most commonly associated with high relief limestone or sandstone reef', with sandy substrata and mixed rock-and-sand surf zones also used. The 'low reef' framing is not in the source.

Mann 2013's False Bay length-weight relation (Wt g = 0.00001148 x TL mm^3.02) gives about 0.83 kg at 40 cm, 2.2 kg at 55 cm and 4.5 kg at 70 cm, so the weights are inflated. The 'male of 80.5 cm and 8.5 kg' merges two separate Mann statements (heaviest fish sampled 8,534 g; longest 805 mm TL). The p

The cited posts give no 'unless you are with a party' exception. The Swartklip post says 'not fishing once the sun starts setting'; the Macassar 2020 post says 'fish during the day - safety reasons'; another says the Strandfontein to Macassar stretch 'should only be visited in groups' at any time. H
This is stated as fact in the habitat text, but the profile's own unverified list admits no source puts belman at The Horses.

A 4 oz grapnel cast into a big sea needs a full surf-casting outfit. That is heavy surf tackle, not the light running-sinker fishing the page covers. The sources do not recommend fishing a big sea at all; they time belman for when the swell drops.
unverified: All condition weights (light, sea, tide, flow, range, trend, clarity, wind) are estimates built from the reports cited. Only the high-tide-at-dawn/dusk timing and the preference for small, settling surf have direct Cape sources.

Night and dusk light weights (0.3 and 0.75) are cut for angler safety on the Swartklip to Macassar stretch, not on fish biology. Night feeding is only inferred from cave-sheltering by day (Mann 2013). The engine should also cap night and late-dusk scores, or show a safety warning, for Swartklip, Strandfontein, Mnandi, Monwabisi and Macassar whatever the species weight.
Water-temperature band (12 / 14 to 19 / 24 C) is an estimate; no thermal study was found
Summer presence on the shore is assumed from residency; no summer shore catches were found in Cape reports
Typical shore size of 40 to 55 cm is an estimate. The weights for each length come from Mann 2013's False Bay length-weight relation, and the maxima from Mann 2013.

Rig specifics (rod length, sinker weights, trace diameters, hook sizes) are an estimate consistent with 'light to medium tackle with scaled-down hooks and leaders' (District Mail) and the author's preferred 3 oz sinker in the same column

The exact location of 'Broken Road' (Jacita, May 2025) was not checked against the Helderberg MPA boundary (Eerste to Lourens river mouths); it is named only as a report location, not as a spot to fish
The WWF-SASSI red listing and the NBA 2018 Near Threatened status were not checked by the reviewer (not in the cache)
FishBase's Umbrina-robinsoni URL resolves to Umbrina ronchus; Mann 2013 says that identification was wrong, so FishBase numbers were not used
No source mentions belman at The Horses; it is listed in the habitat text only as similar ground (inference)

banded-tilapia.name: Banded tilapia (vleikurper)
banded-tilapia.season_note: FishTheFly says 'the best time to catch Vlei Kurper (Banded Tilapia) is during the spring and summer', which is also its breeding season. In the Cape that means October to March, when the weedy shallows warm up. It is in the water all year but slow in cold winter water. Within the 1-hour radius it is confirmed only on the Berg River at Paarl, where a writer for The Mission says his son catches 'small banded Tilapia on a stick rod and float'. Banded tilapia were also seen spawning in clear, flooded grass with bass and carp at Kwaggaskloof Dam near Worcester. That is in the Breede Valley, outside the 1-hour radius. Do not confuse it with Mozambique tilapia, the species the Western Cape government lists for Rietvlei, Zeekoevlei and Sandvlei (Zandvlei). Zeekoevlei is closed to fishing. Rietvlei is open only from 07:30 to 17:00. At Zandvlei the Zandvlei Trust asks anglers to release indigenous fish.

temp.basis: Estimate. FishBase gives only a 22 to 25 C 'tropical' range, and that is an aquarium figure. This species is generally regarded as the most cold-tolerant southern African tilapia, but no source opened this run gives the temperatures at which it stops feeding or dies.

banded-tilapia.habitat: Shallow, weedy, vegetated edges of rivers, dams and vleis. It stays in plant cover in the shallows and does not build up large numbers in deep open water. Spawning fish use flooded grass and shallow margins in clear water. Pairs guard eggs laid on the bottom or stuck to weed.
banded-tilapia.diet: Omnivore. Adults mostly eat filamentous algae, water plants and plant matter that falls in from the land, plus insects and organic detritus. Juveniles eat small crustaceans and midge larvae. Anglers catch it on bits of worm, insects, prawn and small snails, and on small artificial lures.
banded-tilapia.typical_size: Usually 8 to 15 cm (Afrikaans Wikipedia: about 15 cm). A big one is 18 to 23 cm. The maximum is 23.5 cm TL and 445 g (FishBase), and the SA angling record is about 0.31 kg.
banded-tilapia.handling: It has a small spiny dorsal fin. Under the Western Cape ordinance (s57b) you may not sell, buy or transport live banded tilapia without a permit, so do not move it between waters or use it as live bait. You need a CapeNature freshwater angling licence. Do not confuse it with the protected indigenous Cape kurper (Sandelia capensis). Cape kurper is a mottled fish found from mountain streams down to lowland rivers, pools and vleis of the south-western Cape, so it can turn up in the same weedy margins. Banded tilapia has 8 to 9 vertical bars and a dark spot at the base of the soft dorsal fin. If a small perch-like fish has no such spot, treat it as a Cape kurper and release it at once, in the water. CapeNature requires catch-and-release for indigenous freshwater fish. Release Cape kurper, Berg River redfin and witvis at once, with wet hands and in the water. Never target them. Release guarding parents quickly so the brood survives. It is a good first fish for children.

tactics.title: Stick float and a bit of worm in the weedy shallows
tactics.lure_or_bait: Small piece of earthworm, a maggot or a pinch of bread
tactics.retrieve: Still. Strike at small taps, because the mouth is small.
tactics.depth: Bait 10 to 20 cm above the weed or bottom in 0.5 to 1.5 m
tactics.stand: A weedy margin or reed edge with open pockets close in
tactics.rig: #12 to #14 hook, 2 kg mono, small stick or quill float, 1 to 2 split shot
tactics.why: On the Berg River at Paarl, a writer for The Mission says his son catches 'small banded Tilapia on a stick rod and float'. Afrikaans Wikipedia lists bits of worm, insects, prawns and small snails as baits.

tactics.title: Tiny nymph along the warm weed edge
tactics.lure_or_bait: PTN, GRHE, Zak or Orange Hotspot nymph, #14 to #18
tactics.retrieve: Slow figure-of-eight or short slow strips with pauses. FishTheFly says 'all sorts of retrieves can work', but keep the fly small.
tactics.depth: 0.3 to 1 m, along the weed line
tactics.stand: The sunny bank, with weed edges and open pockets within casting range
tactics.rig: 0 to 2 wt rod, floating or intermediate line, 9 ft leader to 5X (about 2 to 3 kg) tippet
tactics.why: FishTheFly says 'small flies are the key', that nymphing methods used for trout and yellowfish work, and suggests a 0 to 2 wt rod with floating or intermediate line.

tactics.title: Sight-fish the flooded grass in spawning season
tactics.lure_or_bait: Small Woolly Bugger, Red-Eyed Damsel or Fritz, #12 to #14
tactics.retrieve: Drop the fly beside the guarded spot, let it sink, then give short twitches. Paired fish chase off intruders.
tactics.stand: A high bank or dry ground above flooded grass and shallow bays. Wear polarised glasses.
tactics.rig: 2 to 3 wt rod, floating line, 5X tippet
tactics.why: At Kwaggaskloof Dam near Worcester, The Mission saw 'banded tilapia ... spawning in grass that got flooded by clear water', which gave 'brilliant sight fishing'. That dam is in the Breede Valley, outside the 1-hour radius, so this is Western Cape evidence and not from a spot near Cape Town. Within the radius, banded tilapia is confirmed only on the Berg River at Paarl. The flies are from FishTheFly's banded tilapia list.

tactics.title: Worm on the bottom in coloured water
tactics.lure_or_bait: Piece of earthworm or a small bit of prawn
tactics.retrieve: Still. Watch the rod tip or the line for small taps.
tactics.depth: On the bottom next to weed, 0.5 to 2 m
tactics.stand: A slack corner or reed edge, away from the main inflow
tactics.rig: 3 to 5 g running sinker above a small swivel, 30 cm trace to a #12 hook
tactics.why: A scent bait on the bottom finds the fish when they cannot see a fly. The baits are from Afrikaans Wikipedia. The method is an estimate.

tactics.title: Midday in the sheltered, sun-warmed shallows
tactics.lure_or_bait: A single maggot or a tiny piece of worm
tactics.retrieve: Still, with very light float shotting so the slow bites show
tactics.depth: 0.3 to 1 m in the warmest water
tactics.stand: The sheltered shallows on the {upwind} bank, out of the wind. Fish from about 11:00 to 15:00. This is an estimate: on a still, sunny winter day the sheltered bank is assumed to warm fastest.
tactics.rig: #14 hook, 1.5 to 2 kg mono, small float shotted right down
tactics.why: Estimate: a warm-water cichlid slows down a lot in cold water and feeds mainly where and when the water is warmest.

tactics.title: Micro jig for active schools
tactics.lure_or_bait: 1 g micro jighead with a 2 to 3 cm grub or maggot-style soft plastic, which can be tipped with a maggot
tactics.retrieve: Small hops and a slow drop past the weed tops
tactics.depth: 0.3 to 1 m
tactics.stand: Weed edges and the mouths of reed bays
tactics.rig: Ultralight rod, 2 kg line
tactics.why: Afrikaans Wikipedia says it 'takes artificial bait readily'. Before and during breeding the fish can form schools. The rig is an estimate.

legal.bag_note: No bag or size limit (translocated into the south-western Cape).
legal.release: Putting it straight back into the same water is allowed; never move live fish.
legal.quote: Ordinance s57: "No person shall without a permit-- ... (b) sell, buy or transport any live carp, bluegill sunfish, trout, black bass, banded tilapia or exotic invertebrate freshwater fauna"

banded-tilapia.review: Checked by an independent skeptic; 11 corrections applied
review_points: This understates where the protected Cape kurper lives. It also occurs in lowland rivers, pools and wetlands of the south-western Cape, which are the same weedy margins where anglers would be float-fishing for vleikurper. Telling anglers that it lives only in mountain streams makes a misidentified C

This is an unsourced estimate presented as fact. Wind drifts the warm surface layer toward the downwind bank, so in a breeze the upwind shallows are not reliably the warmest. The tactic's basis is already 'estimate', but the stand text states a mechanism as fact.

Kwaggaskloof Dam is in the Breede Valley near Worcester, outside the page's one-hour radius. The only in-radius record is the Berg River at Paarl (float fishing for small fish). The sight-fishing tactic is therefore Western Cape evidence, not evidence from a Cape Town spot.
unverified: The temperature thresholds (min 14, ideal 20 to 28, max 32 C) are estimates. FishBase's 22 to 25 C is an aquarium range.

Banded tilapia is not confirmed at any Cape Flats vlei. Sealine 'kurper' reports at Rietvlei and Zandvlei may be Mozambique tilapia, which is the species the Western Cape government lists there. Within the 1-hour radius, presence is confirmed only on the Berg River at Paarl.
The flooded-grass sight-fishing tactic is based on Kwaggaskloof Dam (Breede Valley, near Worcester), which is outside the 1-hour radius. It has not been seen at any water near Cape Town.

That the protected Cape kurper (Sandelia capensis) also lives in lowland rivers, pools and vleis is from general knowledge (Skelton, Freshwater Fishes of Southern Africa). No source opened this run states it.

That banded tilapia is translocated (not native) in the Western Cape is from general knowledge. No source opened this run states it. A text search of the cached Gazette did not find it on the 2020 NEM:BA national list.
The spawn months (October to February) were mapped from FishTheFly's 'spring and summer'.
All light, trend, clarity, wind and flow weights are estimates.
The cold-water midday tactic, its choice of the sheltered {upwind} bank, and the bottom-bait-in-coloured-water rule are estimates.
The web search budget ran out this run, so no account of its cold tolerance from Skelton or SAIAB could be found.

barbel.name: Barbel (sharptooth catfish)
barbel.season_note: Barbel are confirmed all year in Sandvlei/Zandvlei and the lower Liesbeek, where the Western Cape Government lists them in large numbers. At Rietvlei they appear only in the reserve's rule that carp and barbel must be removed. The official species list gives Rietvlei as carp and Mozambique tilapia only, so barbel there are possible but not established. Zeekoevlei also holds barbel but is closed to fishing. The City suspended fishing there over mercury and lead in the fish, then closed it again after a sewage spill in December 2025, so do not fish it. Barbel bite best in warm water, from late spring to early autumn. In winter (June to August) the vleis cool and the bite slows to a trickle (estimate). On spawning, The Mission describes a spawning-like catfish run in a Cape trout stream, and catfish spawning in newly flooded grass at Quaggaskloof, but gives no month for either. In their native range they spawn in the rainy season on flooded ground (FishBase). The Cape's rain falls in winter, so the October to February spawning window here is an estimate based on water temperature. Rietvlei is open only from 07:30 to 17:00, so for most of the year dusk and night fishing are not possible there; fish the last hours before closing. Zandvlei's mouth is often closed in summer. Barbel there sit in the vlei itself, so tide makes little difference.

temp.basis: FishBase gives a survival range of 8 to 35 C (subtropical). The feeding thresholds are estimates: below about 12 C the bite is very slow, it is best from about 20 C, and they keep feeding into the low 30s. The figure that Cape vleis rarely go above about 26 C is also an estimate, not a measured value.

barbel.habitat: Shallow, calm, swampy water over soft mud (FishBase), plus weed mats and reed fringes. In rivers they sit in the slow lower reaches and deeper pools. The Western Cape Government lists sharptooth catfish in large numbers in the lower Liesbeek, and also in Sandvlei/Zandvlei. At Garden Route Dam near George, outside this page's area, The Mission found them in weed gaps and at a pipe outflow that was discharging sewage. That is not a model for Cape Town spots. They gather to spawn in newly flooded grass (The Mission, Quaggaskloof) and in shallow runs and tailouts (The Mission, an unnamed Cape trout stream). Air-breathing organs let them live in warm, low-oxygen urban water (Wikipedia). Zeekoevlei holds them but is closed to fishing. At Rietvlei they are named only in the reserve's removal rule; the official species list there is carp and Mozambique tilapia.
barbel.diet: Mainly a predator on crustaceans, insects and fish, feeding at night (FishBase). It also scavenges living and dead animal matter, eats fruit and seeds, and has taken waterbirds (Wikipedia). At Zandvlei anglers have caught them on mullet bait (Sealine). They find food mostly by touch and smell through their whiskers, so scented baits outfish lures.
barbel.typical_size: From the shore in Cape vleis and the lower Liesbeek, usually 1 to 5 kg, about 60 to 80 cm (estimate). A big one is 10 kg or more and about a metre long; The Mission reports a fish of almost 1 m on fly at Garden Route Dam (George). FishBase gives a common length of 90 cm and a species maximum of 170 cm and 60 kg.
barbel.handling: Do not lip barbel with bare hands. The rough tooth pads draw blood: The Mission's author cut his hands lipping one and later thought about antibiotics. Clean any cuts, especially after fishing urban water. The pectoral fins carry stout spines and the fish is very slimy. Hold it with a wet towel behind the head, clear of the pectoral spines, or use a lip grip, and unhook with long pliers. Barbel are an invasive alien that threatens indigenous fish (City of Cape Town). At Rietvlei, carp and barbel must be removed from the water and not returned, and indigenous fish must go back (Friends of Rietvlei rules). Elsewhere, follow your CapeNature licence conditions. Never move a live fish to another water: that needs a permit (City of Cape Town, CapeNature). If you keep one, kill it quickly with a firm blow or a spike to the top of the head. Zeekoevlei is closed to fishing. The City suspended fishing there over mercury and lead in fish tissue (GroundUp) and closed it again after a sewage spill on 31 December 2025 (IOL). Think twice before eating barbel from the Liesbeek or other urban water. Public waters need a CapeNature freshwater angling licence. Zandvlei is an estuary, so carry a DFFE recreational angling permit there as well as the CapeNature licence. Catching harders for bait also needs the DFFE permit, and the harder bag limit applies. Rietvlei caps line at 4.5 kg breaking strain, two rods per angler and two hooks per rod. At Zandvlei the Zandvlei Trust asks that indigenous fish be released. Return any indigenous fish you catch unharmed, such as the Red Data Cape galaxias recorded there.

tactics.title: Night bait on the mud
tactics.lure_or_bait: Thumb-sized chunk of chicken liver (tie it on with bait elastic), sardine, or a chunk of harder (mullet). A bunch of earthworms also works. Use dead bait only. Buy harders, or catch them in the sea on rod and line under a DFFE recreational angling permit and within the bag limit. Do not net them, and do not take harders from Zandvlei, where indigenous fish should be released.
tactics.rig: Size 1/0 to 2/0 circle hook on a 30 cm trace of 0.45 mm (about 15 kg) mono to resist the tooth pads. 10 to 20 g running ball sinker above a swivel, on 0.30 to 0.35 mm main line. At Rietvlei the whole rig must be 4.5 kg or lighter, and the reserve is closed at night (open 07:30 to 17:00).
tactics.retrieve: No retrieve. Leave it on the bottom with the bail open or the drag very light. When line runs off, give it 2 to 3 seconds, then close the bail and wind down. With a circle hook, do not strike.
tactics.depth: On the bottom, 0.5 to 2 m in the margins
tactics.stand: Soft muddy margins and reed edges where shallow water drops into deeper water. In the Liesbeek, the slow, deeper pools of the lower reaches. Not at Rietvlei, which closes at 17:00, and never at Zeekoevlei, which is closed to fishing. Night fishing in urban rivers and vleis carries a personal-safety risk, so go in company.
tactics.why: They feed at night on almost anything, living or dead (FishBase, Wikipedia), and anglers at Zandvlei have caught them on mullet (Sealine). Scent does the work in the dark. Dusk and night are only possible at waters with no closing time.

tactics.title: Weedless rattle fly over the weed
tactics.lure_or_bait: Bushy, almost fully weedless fly with a built-in rattle that pushes water and sinks slowly (The Mission's 'Catfish Mop' style). Black or dark olive, size 1/0 to 2/0 (colour and size are estimates).
tactics.rig: 6 to 8 weight rod, floating line, 20 lb tippet with the drag locked (The Mission used a 6 weight and 20 lb). At Rietvlei, drop to a 4.5 kg tippet and finish by the 17:00 closing.
tactics.retrieve: Cast into gaps in the weed where whiskers show and let the fly sink into the gap. Then shake the rod tip or give short, sharp tugs to work the rattle. Takes come close to the surface.
tactics.depth: Surface to 0.5 m, in gaps in surface weed
tactics.stand: On the bank beside surface weed mats or reed beds. Watch for whiskers poking through the weed and cast to them.
tactics.why: This is the Garden Route Dam (George) method and has not been tested in Cape Town vleis. There it was fished from late afternoon until dark (The Mission). Blind fishing in open water was 'pointless'; fishing the weed gaps where fish showed produced fish up to almost a metre. The dusk and dull-day triggers are an estimate.

tactics.title: Sight-fish the spawning shallows
tactics.lure_or_bait: A nymph (Flemming's fish took a nymph on a dry-dropper), or a weighted black Woolly Bugger-style barbel fly such as the Babich Barbel Bugger. Size 4 to 8 and the colour are estimates.
tactics.rig: 5 to 7 weight rod, floating line, 0.20 to 0.28 mm (about 2X to 0X) tippet (rod and tippet are estimates), 4.5 kg maximum at Rietvlei
tactics.retrieve: Cast well ahead of a cruising or rooting fish, let the fly drop in front of its head, then give slow short strips along the bottom. Strike on any line movement.
tactics.depth: 0.2 to 0.8 m: shallow runs, tailouts and flooded grass
tactics.stand: Walk the bank quietly with polarised glasses and the light behind you, looking for fish in shallow runs, tailouts, flooded grass and shallow muddy margins. Do not wade in urban rivers or vleis. The sources describe a Cape trout stream and Quaggaskloof Dam, not Cape Town vleis, so where to stand here is an estimate.
tactics.why: Leonard Flemming saw a spawning-like catfish run in the shallow runs and tailouts of a Cape trout stream, and caught one by accident on a nymph while trout fishing. Catfish also spawn in grass newly flooded by clear water (The Mission, Quaggaskloof). Neither source gives a month, so the October to February window is an estimate. Barbel on fly is an established pursuit in South Africa (Babich Barbel Bugger).

tactics.title: Slow scented soft plastic on the bottom
tactics.lure_or_bait: 3 to 4 inch paddle-tail or creature bait in black, purple or motor oil, with scent added, on a 7 to 10 g jighead, size 1/0 to 2/0
tactics.rig: 0.25 to 0.30 mm mono or 10 to 15 lb braid with a 60 cm 0.40 mm mono leader (keep everything at 4.5 kg or less at Rietvlei)
tactics.retrieve: Drag and hop it slowly along the mud with long pauses. Most takes come on the drop or while the lure sits still. Re-scent it every few casts.
tactics.depth: Bottom, 0.5 to 2.5 m
tactics.stand: Off points, and along the edge where the shallow margin drops into the main vlei channel or a river pool
tactics.colour: Dark (black, purple, motor oil) for a silhouette in coloured water
sources: estimate: no Cape lure source for barbel found
tactics.why: A lure option for when bait is impractical. Barbel hunt by smell and touch, so a slow, scented lure on the bottom works best. This is an estimate, not from a Cape source.

tactics.title: Fish the wind-blown bank
tactics.lure_or_bait: Earthworm bunch or chicken liver
tactics.rig: Size 1/0 circle hook, 30 cm trace of 0.40 to 0.45 mm mono (4.5 kg maximum at Rietvlei), 10 to 20 g running sinker
tactics.retrieve: No retrieve. Leave it on the bottom and wind down when the line runs.
tactics.depth: Bottom, 0.5 to 1.5 m
tactics.stand: {downwind}: fish the muddy shallows and reed edges there, where stirred-up water and drifting food collect
tactics.why: A steady breeze stirs and colours the shallows on the wind-blown bank and concentrates food there, and barbel feed by smell and touch. This is an estimate.

tactics.title: Bright day: shade and depth
tactics.lure_or_bait: Earthworm bunch or chicken liver
tactics.rig: Size 1 to 1/0 circle hook, 30 cm trace of 0.40 mm mono, 15 g running sinker (4.5 kg maximum at Rietvlei)
tactics.retrieve: No retrieve. Leave it on the bottom; expect few bites.
tactics.depth: Bottom of the deepest water nearby, 1.5 to 3 m
tactics.stand: Shaded water under bridges, overhanging trees and reed walls, or the deepest pool of the lower river
tactics.why: Barbel feed at night (FishBase), so in bright sun the odds are low. If you must fish, put a scented bait in front of fish resting in shade and deep water. Where to stand is an estimate.

tactics.title: Cold water: small and slow
tactics.lure_or_bait: A small bunch of earthworms
tactics.rig: Size 2 to 1 hook, 20 cm trace of 0.35 mm mono, lightest running sinker that will cast (5 to 10 g)
tactics.retrieve: No retrieve. Leave it; bites are slow and gentle, so watch the line closely.
tactics.depth: Bottom, 0.5 to 1.5 m
tactics.stand: Shallow, sheltered bays or banks that catch the afternoon sun and warm first. Fish the warmest part of the day, not the night.
tactics.why: In winter, Cape vlei water falls well below the barbel's comfortable feeding range. Small baits in the warmest water give you the only realistic chance. This is an estimate.

tactics.title: Late-afternoon bait on the bottom
tactics.lure_or_bait: Chicken liver, sardine or a harder chunk (bought, or caught in the sea under a DFFE permit), or a bunch of earthworms
tactics.rig: Size 1/0 to 2/0 circle hook on a 30 cm trace of 0.40 to 0.45 mm mono, 10 to 20 g running ball sinker, 0.30 to 0.35 mm main line. At Rietvlei keep the whole rig at 4.5 kg or less, with no more than two hooks per rod.
tactics.retrieve: No retrieve. Leave it on the bottom with a light drag or an open bail. When line runs, wait 2 to 3 seconds, then wind down.
tactics.depth: On the bottom, 0.5 to 2 m
tactics.stand: Soft muddy margins, reed edges and the drop-off into deeper water. In the Liesbeek, the slow pools of the lower reaches. Not Zeekoevlei, which is closed to fishing.
tactics.why: Barbel are bottom-feeding scavenger-predators that find food by smell (FishBase). A scented bait on the mud from late afternoon into dusk is the most reliable light-tackle method. At Rietvlei, fish the last hours before the 17:00 closing; dusk and night are only possible at waters with no closing time.

Cape Town sunset runs from about 17:45 (June) to about 19:58 (December), so the engine's dusk window (an hour either side of sunset) starts after 17:00 for most of the year and is only partly open in mid-winter. The dusk-weighted fly tactic and the

The Quaggaskloof spawning was 'in grass that got flooded by clear water', not coloured water. No cited source links rain or colo

blacktail.name: Blacktail (dassie)
blacktail.season_note: Blacktail live on Cape rocks all year. WWF-SASSI calls them a 'residential' fish of shallow rocky ground, so sea state and safety matter more than the month. Sealine threads posted in December (Kogelbaai: blacktail 'plentiful', prawn the best bait), September (Glencairn Quarry: 'dassies on low tide') and November (rocks below Clovelly station) mention blacktail, but those months are when the threads were posted, not when the fish were caught. The only dated catch reports found are from late autumn and winter: Strand in June 2012 ('plentiful and fat'), Jacita in May 2025 (kolstert active at Macassar, Broken Road and Betty's Bay, best on high tide) and Jacita in June 2025 ('calm seas and some blacktail'). The March to June peak is a low-confidence estimate based on those three reports. Expect fish in any month. The Western Cape government page lists blacktail at Melkbosstrand and Rooikrans. Cape Point is the documented western edge of the main South African population (Wikipedia, citing Mann et al. 2014), so Atlantic-side spots such as Melkbos probably hold fewer fish than the False Bay rocks. Eastern Cape spawning runs August to March and peaks September to December. The Cape spawning months given here are extrapolated from that.

temp.basis: estimate. No measured feeding range was found, and FishBase gives no temperature data. The species ranges from the cold Benguela coast (southern Angola, Namibia) to warm Mozambique water, so it tolerates a wide band. A Springer paper (s10641-023-01396-z) reportedly finds that Benguela fish spawn only below 20 C, but this was seen only in a search snippet and could not be verified. The minimum is set at 10 C because blacktail are reported at Melkbosstrand, where Atlantic-side water often sits at 10 to 12 C during summer upwelling. The ideal band matches typical False Bay summer-autumn water. The maximum rarely matters at Cape Town.

blacktail.habitat: Shallow rocky reef and the white-water wash zone: gullies, kelp-fringed channels, wave-washed points, intertidal ledges and flats, harbour walls and quarry ledges. Usually within a few metres of the rocks in 0.4 to 5 m of water (species range 0 to 50 m, FishBase). A 1992 Rhodes University MSc, seen only as a search snippet, describes it as an abundant inshore species that 'favours turbulent seas and rocky shores', but Cape reports also find it in calm seas. Adults also forage over sand next to reef. Juveniles use tidal pools, estuary mouths and the surf zone. A Zandvlei Trust reminiscence says dassies historically turned up at Zandvlei's mouth as surprise catches. That mouth is often closed in summer, and the Trust asks that indigenous fish caught there, blacktail included, be released. At the page's spots: the rocks below Clovelly station, the Glencairn Quarry ledges, reef patches off Melkbos and the Swartklip–Macassar False Bay stretch. Fish the Strandfontein–Swartklip–Macassar stretch only in a group and avoid it at night. At Macassar, stay west of the Eerste River mouth: the Helderberg MPA, from the Eerste to the Lourens river mouth, is a no-take zone.
blacktail.diet: Omnivore: seaweed, sponges, bivalves (mussels), red bait, crustaceans (prawns, crabs), polychaete worms, other molluscs and small fish (FishBase). Fly anglers imitate red bait (orange flies) and prawns (pink flies). Cape anglers rate prawn the best blacktail bait (a Kogelbaai regular: prawn 'will catch most of the species, especially blacktail'), followed by red bait, mussel and worms.
blacktail.typical_size: Usually 20 to 30 cm TL, roughly 200 to 500 g (FishBase common length 30 cm TL). A big one is 38 to 45 cm, about 1.5 to 2 kg (FishBase max 45 cm TL). The 2 kg figure comes from a 1971 Farmer's Weekly line ('big blacktail (anything up to 2 kg)'), which uses the Eastern Cape/KZN sense of the name. FishBase gives maturity at about 21 cm and a maximum age of 21 years.
blacktail.handling: Recreational-only, no-sale species (WWF-SASSI Red, 'don't buy'). Bag limit 5 per person per day; minimum size 20 cm TL. Sharp dorsal and anal spines: grip from the front and smooth the dorsal fin down. Strong crushing teeth: keep fingers out of the mouth. Measure quickly. Release undersize fish head-first into calm water beside the rocks with wet hands, and keep them off hot rock. The same baits and spots catch galjoen, which are closed from 15 October to the last day of February and must be released at once during that period. Stay out of the no-take MPA zones: St James, Boulders, Castle Rock (Miller's Point to Partridge Point), Paulsberg, Cape of Good Hope (Scarborough to Hoek van die Bobbejaan), Karbonkelberg (Oudekraal to Hout Bay) and the Helderberg MPA (Eerste to Lourens river mouths). At Zandvlei the Zandvlei Trust asks that indigenous fish, blacktail included, be released. Do not strip red bait off reefs where that is prohibited; Strand anglers call it a 'big NO NO' there.

tactics.title: Float a prawn through the wash
tactics.lure_or_bait: Peeled prawn tail, a thumbnail of fresh red bait or a mussel on a #2 to 1/0 short-shank hook
tactics.rig: 10 to 20 g bung or wash float, 50 to 80 cm of 0.30 to 0.35 mm fluorocarbon trace, single #2 to 1/0 hook, one small split shot only if the bait rides up; 8 to 10 ft light rod, 15 to 20 lb line
tactics.retrieve: Let the backwash and foam lines carry the float along the reef edge, recast up-current after each drift, and strike on the first firm dip
tactics.depth: 0.5 to 1.5 m under the surface, just above the kelp and rock
tactics.stand: A safe ledge well above the wash, beside a gully mouth or a sheltered point, casting into the edge of the white water. If sets reach your ledge, move back or leave. Never turn your back to the sea.
tactics.why: Estimate, low confidence: no cited source describes float-fishing for blacktail around Cape Town. The reasoning: blacktail feed in turbulent water over rock, where waves knock loose red bait, mussels and crustaceans (a 1992 Rhodes MSc, seen only as a search snippet, says they favour 'turbulent seas and rocky shores'). A Kogelbaai regular says prawn 'will catch most of the species, especially blacktail'. A float keeps the bait above the kelp, where a sinker would snag.
sources: estimate: no Cape source for float-fishing blacktail

tactics.title: Slack-water drift line in the gully
tactics.lure_or_bait: Mussel, red bait, wonderworm or a sliced chokka strip; two hooks with a different bait on each
tactics.rig: No sinker: 0.30 mm line or trace straight to a #1 or 1/0 hook; the bait is the weight (drift line). One split shot only if surge lifts it. 8 to 10 ft light rod
tactics.retrieve: Lob it into the gully, let it sink naturally on a slack line, keep in touch with it and lift into any weight; re-bait often
tactics.depth: Sinking through mid-water to the bottom of a 1 to 3 m gully
tactics.stand: On the rock above a deep, sheltered gully or quarry ledge at low water, such as the Glencairn Quarry face or the rocks below Clovelly station
tactics.why: Glencairn Quarry anglers report 'dassies on low tide' on unweighted drift lines baited with mussel, wonderworm and chokka. They warn that a drift line 'won't work too well in moving water', meaning current, so the method suits slack water around low tide in a sheltered gully. Limiting it to flat or small seas is an estimate: surge lifts an unweighted bait too.

tactics.title: Sight-cast a fly to tailing fish on the push
tactics.lure_or_bait: Octane Orange red-bait fly (a Port Elizabeth pattern; hook size #8 to #4 and bead-chain eyes are estimates), or a Steve Austin pink prawn fly on a #10 shrimp hook with a tungsten dumbbell
tactics.rig: 5 to 7 weight rod (estimate) and floating line. Leader, per the Port Elizabeth pattern notes: 9 ft with about 45 cm (18 in) of 10 lb tippet, or in very shallow water 7 ft with 25 to 30 cm (10 to 12 in) of 8 lb tippet
tactics.retrieve: Port Elizabeth (Eastern Cape) technique: drop the fly within 75 cm of tailing fish, let it settle about 5 seconds, then retrieve with a slow figure-of-eight. The take usually comes in the first metre
tactics.depth: Intertidal ledges and flats in 40 cm of water or less
tactics.stand: Stay low, 15 to 20 m back from the feeding fish, working along the edge of the flat as the tide pushes in. Check that the flat is outside the no-take zones (St James, Boulders, Castle Rock and the others listed under handling).
tactics.why: Cape basis: Conrad Botes, called one of the pioneers of fly fishing for blacktail in the Western Cape, fishes his prawn fly on intertidal flats 'with the incoming tide, just when all the critters that it imitates are active'. The Mission calls that fly the 'scourge of wildeperd and blacktail alike'. The approach to tailing fish, the leader and the retrieve come from a Port Elizabeth (Eastern Cape) pattern write-up. These sources do not say which Peninsula or False Bay flats hold tailing blacktail.

tactics.title: Weighted fly in the washing machine
tactics.lure_or_bait: The same orange red-bait fly; a small Clouser or Fritz gully fly, #6 to #2, is an estimated alternative
tactics.rig: Two lead split shot crimped 30 to 38 cm (12 to 15 in) above the fly, 10 lb tippet. The 6 to 8 weight rod and the floating or intermediate line are estimates
tactics.retrieve: Let it tumble in the wash on a tight line and give short strips between surges; hold on as the backwash pulls
tactics.depth: Near the bottom of the gully, 0.5 to 2 m
tactics.stand: Beside a gully or channel that fills and drains with each wave, on a ledge the sets do not wash over. Never turn your back to the sea, and leave if the sets start reaching you.
tactics.why: For deeper gullies and the 'washing machine', the FOSAF pattern notes (Port Elizabeth) say to add two split shot 12 to 15 inches from the fly. Fish The Fly lists blacktail among its gully-fly targets (search snippet only). The rod weight, line and alternative patterns are estimates.

tactics.title: Scent bait on the reef edge in coloured water
tactics.lure_or_bait: Bloodworm, wonderworm or prawn on a #1 to 1/0 hook; a mixed bait of worm and prawn
tactics.rig: 30 to 60 g running sinker on a weak-link (rotten-bottom) sinker trace to save the rig in kelp, 50 cm trace of 0.35 mm, single hook; 9 to 10 ft light rod
tactics.retrieve: Cast to where reef meets sand, keep a tight line and drag a metre at a time, pausing long between moves
tactics.depth: On the bottom, 1 to 4 m
tactics.stand: At the edge of the foam where reef meets sand, ideally fished up into the high tide. At Macassar, fish only west of the Eerste River mouth (the Helderberg MPA is no-take), and fish the Strandfontein–Macassar stretch in a group, never at night.
tactics.why: Estimate: the idea that blacktail find food by scent more than sight in coloured water is an inference, not from a source. Jacita's May 2025 report, which says nothing about water colour, had kolstert active at Macassar, Broken Road and Betty's Bay 'especially on high tide' on bloodworm and mixed baits. That supports the high-tide timing and the baits. A Kogelbaai regular says wonderworm is 'worth trying'. Rooi-Els advice is to use a strong trace because the kelp snags.
sources: estimate: coloured-water scent feeding is an inference

tactics.title: Rough sea: a sheltered harbour wall or nothing
tactics.lure_or_bait: Prawn, red bait or mussel on a #1 hook
tactics.rig: 20 to 40 g running sinker or a float, 0.35 mm trace, #1 hook; 9 to 10 ft light rod to keep the line off the wall
tactics.retrieve: Short lob into the calm water inside the harbour; let the bait sit and move it only when it snags
tactics.depth: On or just off the bottom, 1 to 3 m
tactics.stand: Inside a harbour such as Gordon's Bay, on a wall the swell does not reach, well back from the edge. Stay off open rock ledges and points entirely in a rough sea. If no sheltered harbour is within reach, do not fish.
tactics.why: A rough sea is not an opportunity on the rocks. Exposed ledges are dangerous (Rooi-Els guidance warns of rogue waves) and a bait will not hold there. Strand anglers report blacktail inside Gordon's Bay harbour, so a sheltered harbour is the only option this page suggests on rough days.

tactics.title: Night bait for the bigger fish
tactics.lure_or_bait: Prawn or a chokka strip on a 1/0 hook
tactics.rig: Light running sinker 20 to 40 g, 50 cm trace of 0.35 mm, 1/0 hook; 9 to 10 ft light rod
tactics.retrieve: Cast to the edge of the reef and wait; slow drag only if crabs strip the bait
tactics.depth: On the bottom next to the reef, 1 to 3 m
tactics.stand: A well-known, lit, easy-access harbour wall or ledge, fished in a group. Avoid isolated rocks after dark, and skip the Clovelly walkway and the Strandfontein–Macassar stretch at night.
tactics.why: Estimate, not Cape-specific. A 1971 Farmer's Weekly line ('night feeders like stumpnose and big blacktail (anything up to 2 kg) I use a 1/0 hook') uses the Eastern Cape/KZN sense of 'blacktail', and no Cape source supports night feeding. Cape forum regulars warn against secluded spots after dark (2014) and against night fishing on the Clovelly walkway because of crime (2009).

tactics.title: Light bait on the rocks
tactics.lure_or_bait: Prawn, fresh red bait, mussel or worm on a #1 hook
tactics.rig: 9 to 10 ft light rod with a small multiplier or 3000 to 4000 spinning reel, 15 to 20 lb line, 20 to 40 g sinker on a weak-link sinker trace, 50 cm 0.30 to 0.35 mm trace, #1 hook. Cape anglers often use an 11 ft scratch rod, which is above this page's light-tackle limit.
tactics.retrieve: Cast to the edge of the white water beside the reef, keep a tight line and strike on the sharp double knock
tactics.depth: On or just off the bottom, 1 to 3 m
tactics.stand: A safe rock ledge on False Bay or a reef patch off the beach, casting into the wash next to the reef. Stay outside the no-take zones (St James, Boulders, Castle Rock, the Helderberg MPA and the others listed under handling), and fish the Strandfontein–Macassar stretch only in a group.
tactics.why: The standard Cape method for blacktail is bait on light reef tackle. A Cape forum regular recommends scratch tackle for blacktail, hottentot and galjoen. Jacita's June 2025 report had 'calm seas and some blacktail' on red bait, white mussels or worms, and a Kogelbaai regular says prawn catches 'especially blacktail'.

legal.bag_note: 5 per day. Counts toward the aggregate of 10.
legal.note: A and B agree and both match R.959. No closed season. 'Dassie', 'das' and 'kolstert' all mean this fish (R1111 Annexure 10: 'Dassie (blacktail, kolstert)').
