Release of Common carp in any rivers, wetlands, natural lakes and estuaries is prohibited." ... "e. Except for those areas detailed in b above, catch and release of common carp is exempted in discrete catchment systems in w

carp.review: Checked by an independent skeptic; 19 corrections applied
review_points: Flemming (Big Carp Theory, 2020) uses 10 ft and 14 ft rods with 3X fluorocarbon run down the length of the rod and the fly about 1 m below the tip. He gives no 4 to 5 m length and no 15 lb figure. '15 lb' also contradicts '3X': 3X fluorocarbon breaks at roughly 7 to 9 lb, so that number is invented

The source names one rod, a 10 ft 6 in 3 wt; '3 to 5 wt' is an embellishment. The source gives no hook size and no depth ('slightly deeper water'), so #12 to #14 and 1 to 2 m are estimates presented as fact. The venue is a Swartland dam, not one of the page's Cape Town waters. The 4X tippet is sourc

Flemming's 3 kg remark is about winter: on sunny days between cold fronts he 'seldom walked away with a fish bigger than 3 kg'. It is not a general rule for shallow-water fish, and his 2020 piece shows a 21 lb (about 9.5 kg) carp on the 6 wt.

None of the three Flemming pieces checked says this. The 2015 article does not cover crustaceans. The 2018 article says Western Cape carp are warier, take smaller patterns and graze small aquatic invertebrates in silt. The 2020 article says a crayfish pattern landed near carp sent them 'tailing for

Flemming 2015 says only that the season 'usually ends in the Western Cape after the first big cold fronts'. No month appears in the text checked. He also says winter fly fishing is generally not worth the effort. 'Late April or early May' and the peak_months end of 3 are inferences.

City of Cape Town: angling at City dams has been under a moratorium since 2005. Since 2007 Doordekraal allows only limited, controlled fishing from October to April with the relevant permits. The profile leaves out this seasonal closure, so the engine would rate Doordekraal for carp in May to Septem

The source (GroundUp, 17 Oct 2023) supports a suspension from 28 Aug 2023, with all fishing later suspended except organised competitions. Nothing confirms the status in November 2026, so 'has been closed since' states a current fact that was not checked. The mercury and lead results come from Zeeko

The thread reports Eviljohnny's 10 kg night fish and, separately, that he uses TCP mielies. It does not say which bait caught the 10 kg fish. In the same thread Nomad says he never saw a Zandvlei carp over 6 kg. Night access at Zandvlei is unverified: the City's Zandvlei reserve and park pages say n
unverified: temp.min 10 C, temp.ideal_hi 27 C and temp.max 32 C are estimates. Only the FishBase tolerance (3 to 35 C), the FishBase breeding range (15 to 20 C) and Flemming's 'about 20 C' river-activity figure are sourced.

Light weights for night, dawn and dusk: the Cape fly sources favour about 11:00 to 16:00 and call early and late a lull. The night value rests on one forum report of a 10 kg Zandvlei night fish, and the thread doesn't say which bait caught it.

Sea, tide and range weights are estimates (the idea is that carp avoid saline pushes in Zandvlei and Rietvlei); no source covers carp and tides in Cape estuaries. Zandvlei's mouth is often closed in summer, so tide ratings apply there only while it is open.
Pressure-trend weights are estimates; no Cape source links carp bites to air pressure.
Wind weights: the windward-bank advice (Flemming) and wind spoiling sight-fishing (Trakoshis) are sourced; the numbers are estimates.
Flow 0.3 is an estimate. FishBase says slow or still water, but Berg River carp feed in strong current.
Spawn months: only October is observed (Voelvlei 2019). September, November and December are inferred from 'spring and summer' (Fish The Fly) and the 15 to 20 C breeding range.
Peak months November to March, and the late April or May end of the fly season, are inferred. Flemming says only that the season ends after the first big cold fronts and names no month.

Bait hook sizes, sinker weights and line diameters (ledger, night, coloured-water, bread and float tactics) come from general carp practice, not from a Cape source. Only the Rietvlei rod, hook and 4.5 kg line limits are sourced.
Float-fishing for carp (the default tactic) is uncited general practice. The Berg 'stick-and-float' reference was about tilapia, not carp.
Winter pancake tactic: the #12 to #14 hook size and the 1 to 2 m depth are estimates. The source venue is a Swartland dam, not one of the page's Cape Town waters.
Witvis restocking in the Berg is unconfirmed. One writer wondered whether a fish came from 'last summer's stockings', and Trakoshis (2020) says witvis are extinct in the Paarl reach.

Zeekoevlei status is taken from GroundUp (Oct 2023: recreational fishing suspended from 28 Aug 2023, later all fishing except organised competitions) and treated as closed; the November 2026 status was not re-checked. Applying the heavy-metal warning to the Lotus River canal is a precaution, not a measured result.
Typical size 30 to 60 cm and 0.5 to 4 kg is an estimate pieced together from scattered Cape reports.
No cached source confirms carp at Princess Vlei or Little Princess Vlei specifically; the Sealine mention of Little Princess Vlei concerns bass.
Whether carp may be released (rather than must be removed) at venues other than Rietvlei was not checked.

Night access at the listed vleis was not checked except Rietvlei (07:30 to 17:00), Zeekoevlei (closed) and Door De Kraal (October to April with permits; hours not checked). Zandvlei night access is unverified.
The idea that corn and dough are more carp-selective than worms (avoiding indigenous bycatch) is an estimate.

chokka.name: Chokka (squid)
chokka.latin: Loligo reynaudii (also written Loligo vulgaris reynaudii)
chokka.season_note: Chokka are in False Bay all year, but the number that come within reach of the shore changes a lot from year to year. Donavan Cole (Ski-Boat, September 2020, writing about boat fishing) says the Simon's Town to Muizenberg stretch is best from about October to May. Angler Publications calls it a year-round species, 'most prolific in summer'. Shore reports: squid were jigged off the Kalk Bay wall in October 2008 and on 11 to 17 October 2010 (Sealine), and a regular fished the wall 'most nights, mainly for chokka' in 2009. Two other reports show squid were present but are probably boat catches, so they are not shore evidence: Jacita's report for 29 May to 1 June 2025 ('Chokka are in full force around Kalk Bay, Fish Hoek, and Glencairn') does not say shore or boat, and the good winter catches at Buffels Bay are fished from an anchored boat. Some years are thin. A Kalk Bay regular wrote in July 2009: 'No Chokka so far just about all year'. Closed season: the gazetted text (Marine Living Resources Act regulations, Annexure 2 item 4, as amended by R.728 of 2011) gives noon 19 October to noon 23 November. Cole (2020) gives noon 19 October to noon 30 November, and a Sealine poster gave 25 October to 22 November for 2010. DFFE sets these dates by notice and they have changed over the years. Angler Publications also mentions a possible second closure each year. Treat noon 19 October to noon 30 November as closed and check DFFE's current notice. The engine leaves November out, and October counts only up to the 19th. Snoek in False Bay (roughly August to October) bite chokka off the jig (Cole).

temp.basis: ideal_lo comes from Cole (Ski-Boat 2020, boat fishing in False Bay): 'Chokka can usually be caught when water temperatures are from 14°C upwards'. He adds that they go off the bite after a sudden drop in temperature, and he gives no upper limit. A Rhodes University thesis (2000; Eastern Cape commercial jig catches on spawning aggregations, 1991 to 1998; seen only as an abstract in search results) found higher catches at 13 to 18 deg C and the best catch rates at 15.0 to 16.9 deg C. ideal_hi 20, min 12 and max 23 are estimates. Surface water in northern False Bay often runs above 18 deg C during the December to March peak, and an upper ideal of 18 would wrongly score those summer days down.

chokka.habitat: Chokka favour sand or shale bottoms with weed and sea-grass beds next to rock (Cole 2020; Angler Publications: 'usually found over weed beds'), at depths of 5 to 50 m. From the shore you can only reach the shallow edge. Squid move into it at dusk, at dawn and at night, and they come to harbour walls and lit water where baitfish gather. Shore marks named in the sources: the Kalk Bay harbour wall (Sealine 2009 and 2010; Seaside Cottages), and at night with a light, the Simon's Town town jetty and harbour and the Gordon's Bay harbour wall. The night marks come only from Seaside Cottages, a holiday-rental blog with no named angler, so give them low weight. Seaside Cottages also mentions jigging off Fish Hoek beach at sunset. A Sealine local warns that 'Areas in Fish Hoek are MPA', so check the zoning before you try it. Rocky points with sand and weed in front, such as Clovelly or the rocks south of Glencairn Beach at Glencairn Quarry, are estimates: no source names them for chokka. Zoning: (1) The water from the Kalk Bay tidal pool north to the St James tidal pool is the St James no-take zone, so fish the harbour wall south of the tidal pool. (2) The shore from Seaforth (Simon's Town) to Rocklands is the Boulders no-take zone. (3) An older MLRA closed area (regulation 10(f)) runs 500 m out to sea from Jager's Walk, south of Fish Hoek beach, to the northern end of Glencairn Beach. No one has confirmed that it was repealed, so stay out of that stretch. Spawning beds are sausage-shaped bunches of eggs laid on sand, mostly in Eastern Cape bays.
chokka.diet: A predator of small fish. Wikipedia calls it 'an important predator of small fishes'. Locally that means baitfish such as anchovy, juvenile pilchard and maasbanker. It also eats crustaceans and smaller squid. Diet studies of the parent species Loligo vulgaris put fish first, crustaceans second and cephalopods (some of it cannibalism) third. Chokka are eaten by snoek, mackerel, yellowtail, kob and seals. One Sealine poster says Simon's Town mackerel runs are 'usually chasing chokka'.
chokka.typical_size: Cole (2020, boat catches) puts the typical catch at 10 to 30 cm mantle length and says 'Larger specimens of up to 50cm can sometimes be caught.' Squid caught from harbour walls are usually at the small end of that range, roughly 10 to 25 cm mantle and 100 to 300 g. The weights are estimates. A growth study (seen only as a search snippet) gives maximum mantle lengths of 42.5 cm for males and 26.3 cm for females, so the really big ones are males.
chokka.handling: It has no spines or teeth, but it has a sharp beak and squirts ink. Hold it clear of the water for a moment so it inks away from you before you bring it in. Chokka tear off the jig easily. Keep steady pressure, do not pause, and use a drop net off the high Kalk Bay wall. There is no minimum size. The daily bag limit is 20 per person (Cole 2020, Angler Publications 2022 and the older Annexure 6; check DFFE's current notice). You need a recreational fishing permit. Closed season: treat noon 19 October to noon 30 November as closed until you have checked DFFE's current notice. The gazette text says noon 23 November, Cole says noon 30 November, and Angler Publications mentions a second closure each year. To release one, unhook it in the water without squeezing the mantle. To keep one, kill it quickly with a cut or spike between the eyes and keep it cool. Do not fish the St James no-take zone (Kalk Bay tidal pool to St James tidal pool) or the Boulders no-take zone (Seaforth to Rocklands). Stay out of the old regulation 10(f) closed area from Jager's Walk to the northern end of Glencairn Beach until SANParks or DFFE confirms it no longer applies.

tactics.title: Dusk and dawn squid jig off the harbour wall
tactics.lure_or_bait: Size 2.5 to 3.0 egi-style squid jig, about 10 to 15 g
tactics.colour: Cole's order of preference (boat fishing) is pink, blue, white, green, chartreuse/yellow. At Kalk Bay a jig with a pink top and yellow bottom worked, and a small white jig did better (JD, Sealine 2010).
tactics.retrieve: Cast and let it sink almost to the bottom on a tight line. Wind slowly and steadily with the rod tip up, lifting the tip every few turns to feel for weight. Do not jerk it hard: Cole (boat jigging) says to reel steadily without stopping and not to pump the rod. A take feels like extra weight or a bump. Lift into it and keep steady pressure all the way in.
tactics.depth: Lower half of the water, just above the sand and the tops of the weed, 3 to 8 m out from the wall or rocks
tactics.stand: The Kalk Bay harbour wall. Stay south of the Kalk Bay tidal pool: the water from there to St James is a no-take zone. Rocky points with sand and weed in front, such as Clovelly or the rocks south of Glencairn Beach at Glencairn Quarry, are untested estimates.
tactics.rig: Soft-tipped 7 to 8.5 ft spinning rod, 2500 to 3000 reel, 10 to 20 lb braid, 1 to 1.5 m of 10 to 15 lb fluorocarbon leader and a small snap. Set the drag light: braid has no stretch and can tear a squid off the jig.
tactics.why: Chokka come inshore and feed hardest when the light changes. JD at Kalk Bay: 'An hour or two before and after sunset'. Cole, writing about boat fishing, also rates early morning and late afternoon as the best times. Seaside Cottages describes jigging for chokka at sunset.

tactics.title: Night under the lights with a glow jig
tactics.lure_or_bait: Size 2.5 to 3.0 luminous (lumo, glow) squid jig. Recharge it with a torch every few casts. You can also hang it 1 to 2 m under a small float and drift it along the edge of the light (an estimate).
tactics.retrieve: Slower than at dusk. Cast past the edge of the lit water and let it sink. Then wind slowly, pausing for 3 to 5 seconds as it crosses from the light into the dark. Takes often come on the pause.
tactics.depth: Mid-water to just under the surface around the light. Fish deeper if nothing shows within 20 minutes.
tactics.stand: Under the harbour lights on the Kalk Bay wall (south of the Kalk Bay tidal pool). Or shine a light onto the water from the Simon's Town town jetty; do not fish the shore from Seaforth southwards, which is the Boulders no-take zone. Or fish the Gordon's Bay harbour wall, where Seaside Cottages describes lowering a light into the water at night and working the jig slowly.
tactics.rig: As at dusk: light spinning rod, 10 to 20 lb braid with a fluorocarbon leader, snap. Bring a drop net for high walls.
tactics.why: Baitfish gather at lights and squid follow them. Angler Publications advises lumo jigs and a bright light at night, from an anchored boat. Cole (boat) says glow jigs get far more action in the dark. Seaside Cottages describes the same light and luminous-jig method from the Simon's Town and Gordon's Bay harbours. A Kalk Bay regular fished the wall 'most nights, mainly for chokka'.

tactics.title: Overcast afternoon: start early
tactics.lure_or_bait: Size 2.5 to 3.0 squid jig
tactics.retrieve: Cast and let it sink almost to the bottom. Then wind slowly and steadily, lifting the rod tip now and then to feel for weight.
tactics.depth: Lower half of the water, over sand and weed
tactics.stand: The Kalk Bay harbour wall (south of the Kalk Bay tidal pool), casting to the deepest sand edge you can reach. Rocky points such as Clovelly or the rocks at Glencairn Quarry are estimates.
tactics.rig: Light spinning rod, 10 to 20 lb braid, 1 to 1.5 m fluorocarbon leader, snap
tactics.why: Low light brings squid in earlier. JD at Kalk Bay advises fishing around dusk, 'earlier if cloudy'. The colours follow Cole's order of preference (boat fishing).

tactics.title: Bright sun: go deep and slow
tactics.lure_or_bait: Size 3.0 to 3.5 jig (15 to 20 g), or a 2.5 jig with a clip-on lead so it sinks faster
tactics.colour: Natural brown or olive cloth with red or gold foil, or pink
tactics.retrieve: Let it hit the bottom. Then drag it slowly and pause, lifting only 30 to 50 cm, so it stays close to the bottom the whole way back.
tactics.depth: On or just above the bottom, in the deepest water you can reach
tactics.stand: The deepest water within casting range: the seaward side of the Kalk Bay harbour wall, or the rocks at Glencairn Quarry (an estimate). Work any shade lines.
tactics.rig: Light spinning rod, 10 to 20 lb braid, fluorocarbon leader, snap
tactics.why: Expect slow fishing until the light drops. Cole (boat) says the bigger squid are usually in deeper water and the best times are early and late. Angler Publications gives a depth range of 5 to 50 m. Fishing the deepest water near the bottom in bright sun is a shore adaptation of that advice (an estimate).

tactics.title: Weedy low water: floater jig on a running sinker
tactics.lure_or_bait: Floating squid jig (or an unweighted 2.5 egi) on a 60 to 100 cm fluorocarbon leader behind a 10 to 20 g running ball or 'peanut' sinker
tactics.colour: Pink or white, glow after dark
tactics.retrieve: Cast and let the sinker settle. Then drag it slowly with long pauses so the jig hovers just above the weed without snagging it.
tactics.depth: 30 to 80 cm above the bottom, over the weed
tactics.stand: Cast across the sand and weed patches beside the Kalk Bay harbour wall or nearby rocks (south of the Kalk Bay tidal pool), not straight onto kelp
tactics.rig: Running ball sinker on the braid main line, a swivel, then the fluorocarbon leader to the jig
tactics.why: Cole, jigging from a boat at Simon's Town, uses a single floater jig with a peanut-sized sinker when chokka feed near the bottom, where weed and sea grass foul ordinary jigs. Angler Publications says chokka 'are usually found over weed beds'. Using this rig from the shore, and tying it to low tide when the weed is closer to the jig, are estimates.

tactics.title: Swell running: inside the harbour only, or give it a miss
tactics.lure_or_bait: Size 3.0 jig, which holds better in surge than a 2.5
tactics.retrieve: Short casts into calm pockets, a slow wind and long pauses
tactics.depth: Mid-water to the bottom in the calmest pocket
tactics.stand: In a moderate swell, fish only the sheltered inside of a harbour, such as the inner side of Kalk Bay harbour, well back from where waves reach. In a rough sea, do not fish: waves can break over the Kalk Bay outer wall, and wave-washed rocks at Clovelly or Glencairn are dangerous.
tactics.rig: Light spinning rod, 15 to 20 lb braid, fluorocarbon leader, snap
tactics.why: Cole (boat) says a big swell and a strong sea put chokka off the bite. At Kalk Bay, JD stopped expecting squid once the water turned rough. A big swell also stirs up sand and colours the water. Expect a poor session, and in a rough sea stay home.

tactics.title: Coloured water: bright and glowing
tactics.lure_or_bait: Size 2.5 to 3.0 squid jig with a glow body
tactics.colour: Chartreuse, orange or bright pink, with glow
tactics.retrieve: Slower than usual, with long pauses so the squid has time to find it
tactics.depth: Lower half of the water
tactics.stand: The cleanest water you can find, usually the seaward end of the Kalk Bay harbour wall, away from sand churned up by waves or stormwater
tactics.rig: Light spinning rod, 10 to 20 lb braid, fluorocarbon leader, snap
tactics.why: A Rhodes University study of the Eastern Cape commercial jig fishery (abstract only) tied the best catch rates to zero turbidity and found that turbidity breaks up spawning aggregations. Applying that to squid feeding near the shore is an extrapolation. Bright and glowing colours are a common choice for low visibility (an estimate).

tactics.title: Cold snap: deep, small and slow
tactics.lure_or_bait: Small 2.0 to 2.5 squid jig
tactics.colour: White or natural; glow at dusk
tactics.retrieve: Very slow, near the bottom, with long pauses. Fish the dusk window and do not expect much in daylight.
tactics.depth: On or just above the bottom
tactics.stand: The deepest water within casting range: the seaward end of the Kalk Bay harbour wall, or the rocks at Glencairn Quarry (an estimate)
tactics.rig: Light spinning rod, 10 to 15 lb braid, fluorocarbon leader, snap
tactics.why: Cole (boat): 'Chokka can usually be caught when water temperatures are from 14°C upwards'. He adds that they go off after a sudden drop in temperature. In the Eastern Cape fishery (abstract only), catches were higher at 13 to 18 deg C. The small, slow, deep approach is an estimate.

tactics.title: Squid jig from the harbour wall
tactics.lure_or_bait: Size 2.5 to 3.0 egi-style squid jig, about 10 to 15 g
tactics.colour: Pink first, then white, blue, green, chartreuse
tactics.retrieve: Cast and let it sink almost to the bottom. Wind slowly and steadily with the rod tip up, lifting now and then to feel for weight. A take feels like weight or a bump. Keep steady pressure and do not stop winding.
tactics.depth: Lower half of the water, just above the sand and weed
tactics.stand: The Kalk Bay harbour wall, south of the Kalk Bay tidal pool and outside the St James no-take zone, casting toward sand and weed. At night, the Simon's Town town jetty or the Gordon's Bay harbour wall with a light. Rocky points such as Clovelly or the rocks at Glencairn Quarry are estimates. Do not fish Jager's Walk or the coast from there to Glencairn Beach (an old closed area), or Seaforth to Rocklands (the Boulders no-take zone).
tactics.rig: Soft-tipped 7 to 8.5 ft spinning rod, 2500 to 3000 reel, 10 to 20 lb braid, 1 to 1.5 m of 10 to 15 lb fluorocarbon leader, small snap, light drag. A drop net for the Kalk Bay wall.
tactics.why: This is the standard Cape shore method: squid jigs from harbour walls and jetties, best from late afternoon into dark (JD at Kalk Bay; Seaside Cottages). Treat noon 19 October to noon 30 November as closed unless DFFE's current notice says otherwise, and keep to the bag limit of 20.

legal.bag_note: 20 per day. Excluded from the 10-fish aggregate, both because the bag exceeds 10 and because squid is not a fish of the

closed.area: Whole country (no area qualifier in Annexure 2 or in the brochure)
closed.rule: No fishing for or possession of chokka from 12h00 noon on 19 October to 12h00 noon on 23 November (reg 9 with Annexure 2 item 4, as substituted by GN R.728 of 16 Aug 2011; brochure rule (12)).

legal.note: Reconciled: A and B agree on 20 per day, no size limit and the closed season from noon 19 Oct to noon 23 Nov. I confirmed the dates in the cached acts.co.za Annexure 2 item 4 and in brochure rule (12). The Annexure 7 row in R.959 has no closed-season entry for chokka, so the closure binds anglers through reg 9 (which binds 'any person') rather than reg 22. One thing for a human to check: in the co

chokka.review: Checked by an independent skeptic; 21 corrections applied
review_points: None of the cited sources names Clovelly, Jager's Walk or Glencairn Quarry as chokka shore marks. Cole's article is boat-only and names no shore spots. JD's thread does not say which part of the Kalk Bay wall he fished (the summary says 'The harbour wall is not specifically named'), so 'the end of t

The MLRA regulations, section 10(f), list a closed area 500 m seaward of the high-water mark running from a line off 'Jager's Walk situated to the south of Fish Hoek Beach' to the northern boundary of Glencairn Beach, where no one may fish except under a permit. A Sealine local says 'Areas in Fish H

The Jacita report does not say this was shore fishing, and the same sentence credits 'notable boat-based success near Simon's Town'. Buffels Bay chokka are fished 'from an anchored boat' (Angler Publications). Both are boat evidence presented as shore evidence.

The gazette entry is confirmed, but the sources disagree. Cole gives noon 30 November. JD (2010) gave 25 October to 22 November. Angler Publications (2022) says 'there are two closed seasons per year for chokka', and the profile never mentions this. The dates have plainly moved by notice from year t

Cole sets only a lower threshold ('from 14°C upwards') and gives no upper bound. The 13 to 18 and 15 to 16.9 deg C figures come from an Eastern Cape commercial spawning-aggregation fishery, seen only as a search abstract. Northern False Bay surface water in the stated peak months (December to March)

This is a paraphrase in quotation marks. Cole's actual wording is 'Chokka can usually be caught when water temperatures are from 14°C upwards.' The meaning is close, but it should not be presented as a quote.

These are invented numbers that are not listed in unverified. Only the ordering is supported: swell puts squid off (Cole, JD), and dusk and dawn are best (JD, Cole). The coloured 0.2 penalty rests on an Eastern Cape study of turbidity breaking up deep-water spawning aggregations, seen only as an abs

Cole's article is entirely boat-based (anchoring or drifting off Long Beach and Buffels Bay with 1 to 2 oz jigs). The profile never says so, and it uses his advice as if it were shore tactics. The wind remark is about keeping jigs down from an anchored or drifting boat.
unverified: Tide weights (low 0.55, pushing 0.85, high 0.9, dropping 0.7): estimates. No Cape source links shore catches of chokka to the stage of the tide.
Range weights (springs 0.75, neaps 1.0): estimates, based on less current and clearer water at neaps.
Pressure-trend weights: estimates. No source found.
Flow 0.3: estimate. Squid jigging works best in slack, sheltered water, but no source says so.
Wind weights: estimates, partly based on Cole's remark that wind makes jigs hard to keep near the bottom. That remark is about fishing from an anchored or drifting boat.

Temperature: ideal_lo 14 comes from Cole (boat fishing, False Bay). ideal_hi 20, min 12 and max 23 are estimates. The review raised ideal_hi from 18 and max from 21 so that the summer peak is not scored down.

Light weights (night 0.75, dawn 0.85, day_bright 0.25, day_dull 0.5, dusk 1): every number is an estimate. Only the order (dusk and dawn best, then night, bright day worst) is backed by Cape sources (JD, Cole).
Sea weights (flat 1, small 0.85, moderate 0.4, rough 0.1): estimates. Only the order is backed, by Cole (boat) and JD (Kalk Bay), who say swell puts squid off.

Clarity weights (clear 1, coloured 0.4): estimates. The turbidity link comes from an Eastern Cape study of deep-water spawning aggregations, seen only as an abstract. The review cut the coloured penalty from 0.2 to 0.4 because the basis is weak.

Peak months December to May: a blend of 'most prolific in summer', Cole's October to May for Simon's Town (boat) and Jacita's late-May 2025 report (shore or boat not stated). Shore numbers vary a lot from year to year.

Spawn months October to February: based on summer breeding aggregations between Cape Point and Port Elizabeth and on the October to November closures. Little spawning is recorded inside False Bay itself.
Shore spots: no source names Clovelly or the rocks at Glencairn Quarry for chokka, so both are estimates. No source says which part of the Kalk Bay wall fishes best.
Simon's Town town jetty and Gordon's Bay harbour wall as night spots: the only source is Seaside Cottages, a holiday-rental blog with no named angler.

Cole's article is entirely about boat fishing. Every shore use of his advice is an adaptation: the floater rig, bigger squid in deeper water, the colour order, the effect of wind and the 14 deg C threshold.
Shore jig sizes 2.0 to 3.5 and their weights: estimates. Cape sources describe 1 to 2 oz boat jigs or simply 'small' jigs.
Drifting a glow jig under a float at night: estimate.
Natural colours on bright days and chartreuse or orange in coloured water: estimates.
Linking the floater jig on a running sinker to low tide, and using it from the shore: estimates. The rig itself is Cole's boat rig.

Typical weights (100 to 300 g from the shore): estimates. The mantle lengths come from Cole (10 to 30 cm, up to 50 cm). The 42.5 cm and 26.3 cm maximums come only from a search snippet of a growth study.
Specific prey items (anchovy, juvenile pilchard, maasbanker): not confirmed for L. reynaudii. The order of fish first, then crustaceans comes from studies of Loligo vulgaris.

Closed season dates: the gazette text (R.728 of 2011) says noon 19 October to noon 23 November, Cole (2020) says noon 30 November, and JD gave 25 October to 22 November for 2010. The profile uses the most cautious combination, noon 19 October to noon 30 November. Not checked against DFFE's newest notice.
Second annual chokka closure (Angler Publications 2022, 'there are two closed seasons per year'): not confirmed, and the dates are unknown.
Bag limit of 20 a day with no size limit: from Cole (2020), Angler Publications (2022), JD (2010) and the superseded 2005 Annexure 6. Not confirmed in the current gazette.

Zoning: on the TMNP MPA coordinates (Wikipedia), Kalk Bay harbour south of the tidal pool, the Simon's Town town jetty and the Glencairn area are all outside the St James and Boulders no-take zones. That is a coordinate comparison, not an official map. Nobody has confirmed whether the old regulation 10(f) closed area from Jager's Walk to Glencairn Beach still applies. Fish Hoek beach zoning is also unconfirmed: a Sealine local warns that parts of Fish Hoek are MPA.
Jacita May 2025 report and Buffels Bay winter catches: probably boat catches. They show the squid are present but are not evidence from the shore.
Rhodes thesis author and title: only the abstract was seen in search results, because the repository returned 403.

elf.name: Elf (shad)
elf.season_note: Elf visit the Cape in summer. Tagging (Govender 1996, UKZN thesis, abstract only) shows adults move from the Cape to KwaZulu-Natal in winter, where they spawn on the inshore shelf (Beckley & Connell 1996, abstract only). The sources do not say how much of the Cape stock makes the trip, and some fish are back at the Cape by late September: Mattheys (District Mail, 30 Sep 2022) reported 'early-season' elf at Strand, Macassar and towards Strandfontein then. The main shore run is December to February or March (Sealine Muizenberg/Sunrise thread, 2010). At Kalk Bay harbour elf are caught in summer after the south-easter has blown, including over Easter (Sealine 2009). Hangklip and Kleinmond give elf from October to April (villagevoice.co.za). On the Atlantic side (Blouberg, Melkbos, Milnerton), elf turn up only when warmer water is inshore, for example at Melkbos in late February 2025 (Sealine). Elf are scarce from June to August. The closed season runs from 1 October to 30 November. Elf are present and get caught then, but they may not be kept. October and November are left out of present_months so the page does not rank elf as a target in those months. A release rule covers any elf hooked by accident.

temp.basis: min 14 C: Animal Diversity Web says bluefish 'tolerate water temperatures as low as 14°C' (US data; the reviewer did not reopen it). FishBase says the species moves to warmer water in winter and to cooler water in summer. A modelled preferred range of 8.4 to 27.5 C (mean 21.1 C) is NOT on the FishBase summary page. It may come from AquaMaps but is unverified. Cape context: elf come with the summer south-easter, which pushes Agulhas water into False Bay (up to about 20 C, Naysmith, Ski-Boat Nov 2021). At Blouberg, 12 C water gave no bites at all (Sealine 'Spots near Table view', Apr 2024), but that blank covered all fishing, not elf alone. The ideal band of 16 to 21 C and the max of 24 C are estimates.

elf.habitat: Elf hunt in the upper water column of clean, high-energy water. They work surf gutters, rips and white water off sandy beaches (Muizenberg corner to Strandfontein, Macassar, Strand, Milnerton beach, Blouberg, Melkbos), harbour walls (Kalk Bay) and estuary mouths. At Zandvlei they hold near the footbridge and the main island, but only while the mouth is open to the sea; at Milnerton Lagoon they hold on the Woodbridge Island side. Rocky points beside deep water may also hold elf, but no cited Cape source names a rock spot. Shoals follow baitfish into the foam lines, and the south-easter pushes them onto False Bay's north shore. Juveniles use permanently open estuaries (Smale & Kok 1983 found them from September to April in Knysna; abstract only). Stay out of these no-take zones: St James (St James tidal pool to Kalk Bay tidal pool, between Muizenberg and Kalk Bay harbour) and Castle Rock (Miller's Point to Partridge Point); check the TMNP MPA zoning map. The Helderberg MPA bans all fishing between the Eerste River mouth and the Lourens River mouth, out to 500 m from the high-water mark. At Macassar fish only west of the Eerste River mouth, and at Strand only east of the Lourens River mouth.
elf.diet: Piscivore. In the Cape it eats mullet/harders, maasbanker, sardine, anchovy and streepies, plus squid and crustaceans (FishBase). It attacks shoals far beyond its feeding needs (FishBase). Elf are in turn prey for kob and leervis (Mattheys 2022).
elf.typical_size: Typically 30 to 45 cm and 0.5 to 1 kg ('green elf' in shoals; many undersize fish in harbours such as Kalk Bay). A big one is a 'blue elf' of 3 to 5 kg and over 60 cm. Blue elf up to 10 kg have been caught, and the SA record is 10.2 kg from Cape Recife (Mattheys 2024).
elf.handling: Elf have razor-sharp teeth that cut nylon and fingers, and FishBase notes they bite when handled. Use 8 to 10 cm of wire trace and long-nose pliers, and hold the fish behind the head with a wet cloth. Regulations (check the current DFFE rules): minimum size 30 cm, bag limit 4 per person per day, closed season 1 October to 30 November (fish may not be kept). WWF-SASSI rates elf orange. The stock was assessed as overexploited in 1997, and KZN catch rates had not improved after the 2005 rule changes (Maggs, Mann & van der Elst 2012). Release extra and undersize fish quickly, and swap trebles for single hooks to make release easier. At Zandvlei, the Zandvlei Trust asks that indigenous fish, elf included, be released.

tactics.title: Dawn and dusk spoon through the gutter
tactics.lure_or_bait: Slow-sinking silver spoon such as an Abu Toby of 18 to 28 g, or a sinking or sub-surface stickbait (Cid Shiverstick, Rapala sinking) of 15 to 30 g
tactics.retrieve: Cast beyond the white water and count 2 to 3 seconds. Then wind steadily at medium-fast speed, twitching now and then so the lure flashes. Keep it moving; elf chase.
tactics.depth: upper 1 to 2 m, through the foam line
tactics.stand: On the beach, face the deepest gutter or a rip beside a sandbank. From a point or harbour wall, cast along the edge where the swell meets deeper water, but only when swell is not washing over it. At Macassar stay west of the Eerste River mouth, and at Strand stay east of the Lourens River mouth (the Helderberg MPA between them is no-take).
tactics.rig: 8 to 10 ft rod casting 15 to 60 g, 2500 to 4000 reel, 20 lb braid, 1 m of 0.8 mm mono leader (Mattheys gives 0.8 to 1.2 mm), then 8 to 10 cm of piano or plastic-coated wire to a 4/0 single hook
tactics.why: Elf are most active at dawn and dusk, and any silver spoon that does not sink too fast works (Mattheys 2024). The beaches fish best in the evenings (Sealine 2008), and anglers fish the Strand surf for elf early in the morning or at dusk (Seaside Cottages).

tactics.title: Overcast low-tide metal jig
tactics.lure_or_bait: Metal casting jig, e.g. Iron Candy Couta casting 45 g, or a 30 to 35 g slim metal
tactics.retrieve: Cast long with the rod tip low. Wind fast at first, then slow down as the lure reaches the shore break, where most pickups happen.
tactics.depth: mid water up to just under the surface
tactics.stand: On a sandy beach at low tide, cast over the first bank into the outer gutter (estimate; the source does not say where it was fished).
tactics.rig: 9 to 10 ft rod rated to about 60 g, 20 lb braid, 0.8 mm leader, 8 to 10 cm wire, 4/0 single or a single-hook assist
tactics.why: A Sealine regular ('Roachy') fishes the Iron Candy from about 4 pm on overcast days, at low tide in calm seas. He keeps the rod tip low and slows the lure near the shore break, where most fish hit, and calls it his 'not so secret weapon' (Sealine 'Lure fishing the surf', Dec 2013).

tactics.title: High-tide surface lure
tactics.lure_or_bait: Surface walker or popper of 12 to 15 cm and 20 to 30 g (Rapala Skitter Walk or Skitter V class), with the rear treble swapped for a single
tactics.retrieve: Walk the dog fast, or skip the lure across the top.
tactics.depth: surface
tactics.stand: Fish in front of Baileys Cottage / Muizenberg corner on the top of the tide, and stay north of the St James tidal pool: St James to the Kalk Bay tidal pool is a no-take zone. Elsewhere, fish wherever the deep channel comes close to the beach or rocks at high water.
tactics.rig: 8 to 10 ft rod, 20 lb braid, 0.8 mm leader, 8 to 10 cm wire to the lure's split ring
tactics.why: The recommended elf approach at Baileys Cottage is a surface lure or an Iron Candy at high tide (Sealine 2013). Mattheys names Skitter Walk and Skitter V surface lures for the Cape spinning season (Oct 2023).

tactics.title: Churned onshore surf: sardine strip
tactics.lure_or_bait: Fresh sardine (pilchard) fillet, or a mullet or maasbanker strip, cut long and thin, on a 2/0 to 4/0 hook
tactics.retrieve: Cast to the back of the first gutter and let the sinker hold it. Every few minutes, lift and drag it about a metre so the strip flutters.
tactics.depth: bottom to mid water in the gutter
tactics.stand: From a sandy beach only, opposite the deepest gutter or rip, standing well back from the edge of the white water. In rough seas never fish from rocks or harbour walls. This is best on False Bay's north shore (Muizenberg, Strandfontein, Macassar, Strand) after the south-easter has blown warm, coloured water onshore. At Macassar fish only west of the Eerste River mouth, and at Strand only east of the Lourens River mouth: the stretch between the two mouths is the Helderberg MPA, where no fishing is allowed.
tactics.rig: 9 to 10 ft rod casting up to about 85 g. Running trace: 1 to 2 oz grapnel or ball sinker on a slider, swivel, 50 cm of 0.8 mm leader, then 10 cm of wire to the hook. Rough surf may need up to 3 oz to hold, which is the top end of light tackle.
tactics.why: Elf also feed by day 'when the sea is rolling with lots of white water', in water 'a ginger beer colour', and sardine is the most successful bait (Mattheys 2024). Kalk Bay produces elf in summer when the south-easter has been blowing (Sealine 2009). Strandfontein is recommended for bait fishing in rolling waves (Sealine 2008), and fish baits cut long and thin work on the Muizenberg/Sunrise stretch (Sealine 2010).

tactics.title: Estuary mouth on the fly
tactics.lure_or_bait: White or chartreuse-and-white Clouser Minnow or Surf Candy, size 1 to 2/0
tactics.retrieve: Cast across the current and let the fly swing, then strip fast with long, quick strips (two-handed if you can). Pause only briefly.
tactics.depth: top 1 m to mid water in the channel
tactics.stand: Fish the mouth channel. Milnerton Lagoon is the more reliable option: fish the Woodbridge Island side near the prawn pumpers. Fish Zandvlei only when its mouth is open to the sea, which often it is not in summer; then work from the footbridge down to the mouth. The Zandvlei Trust asks that indigenous fish, elf included, be released there. With no current, fish {downwind}, where the wind piles up baitfish.
tactics.rig: 7 to 8 wt rod, intermediate line, 2 m leader of 20 lb, with a 15 cm bite tippet of 40 lb fluorocarbon or fine wire
tactics.why: Sean Mills (Saltwater fly fishing in the W/Cape) says the best area at Zandvlei is near the mouth by the footbridge at sunrise, but that the vlei is 'often closed to the sea in summer'. At Milnerton Lagoon, he names Woodbridge Island as the best spot and says fishing close to the prawn pumpers produces. Fish The Fly calls the Clouser the best surf fly, in white, pink or chartreuse. Elf have been reported at the Zandvlei main island (Sealine 2009 to 2011).

tactics.title: Harbour wall float at dawn and dusk
tactics.lure_or_bait: Strip of fresh sardine or maasbanker on a 2/0 to 4/0 hook (catch the maasbanker first on a sabiki)
tactics.retrieve: Let the running float drift along the wall and past the harbour mouth. Strike when the float runs away, not on the first dip.
tactics.depth: 1 to 2 m under the float (estimate)
tactics.stand: Fish the outer harbour wall at Kalk Bay, on the side where the current and baitfish run along the wall. Do this only in flat or small seas; stay off the wall if swell is breaking over it.
tactics.rig: 9 to 10 ft rod, 15 to 20 lb line, running float with a stopper at 1 to 2 m, small bean sinker, 10 cm wire to the hook
tactics.why: Elf are caught at Kalk Bay harbour in summer after the south-easter, including over Easter (Sealine 2008, 2009; Seaside Cottages). A slider or float setup can tempt elf (Jacita, May 2025). Sardine is the top bait, and dawn and dusk are the most active times (Mattheys 2024).

tactics.title: Cold upwelled water: slow bait or move
tactics.lure_or_bait: Sardine strip on a 2/0 to 4/0 hook, fished slowly. Expect little, and consider another target.
tactics.retrieve: Leave it in the deepest gutter and move it only occasionally
tactics.depth: bottom of the deepest gutter
tactics.stand: Fish the deepest water you can reach from a sandy beach. On the Atlantic side (Blouberg, Melkbos, Milnerton), wait for a westerly to push warmer water back in, or switch to the False Bay north shore.
tactics.rig: Running sinker trace with a 1 to 2 oz grapnel (3 oz at most, the top end of light tackle) and 10 cm of wire
tactics.why: Elf are warm-water summer visitors that leave the Cape in winter (Govender 1996, abstract). At Blouberg, 12 C water gave 'not even a tug' for any species, and a warm west wind brings warmer water back (Sealine 2024).

tactics.title: Closed season: release any elf
tactics.lure_or_bait: Do not target elf. If one takes a lure meant for kob or leervis, release it.
tactics.retrieve: Bring it in quickly and unhook it in the water with long-nose pliers. Do not lift it by the wire.
tactics.depth: n/a
tactics.stand: n/a
tactics.rig: Single hooks with the barbs crushed so the hook comes out quickly
tactics.why: The elf closed season runs from 1 October to 30 November (aquarium.co.za, showme.co.za). The minimum size is 30 cm and the bag limit is 4.

tactics.title: Silver spoon where the gutter runs deepest
tactics.lure_or_bait: Silver spoon of 18 to 28 g (Toby type), or a 30 g metal jig
tactics.retrieve: Wind steadily at medium-fast speed with occasional twitches, fanning casts across the gutter
tactics.depth: upper 2 m
tactics.stand: Wherever the surf gutter, channel or harbour edge runs deepest close in, ideally with some white water or current. Stay off rocks and walls when swell is washing over them.
tactics.rig: 8 to 10 ft rod, 20 lb braid, 0.8 mm leader, 8 to 10 cm wire, 4/0 single hook
tactics.why: Silver spoons and a short wire trace are the standard Cape elf approach (Mattheys 2024).

legal.bag_note: 4 per person per day. Counts toward the overall daily aggregate of 10.

closed.rule: No fishing for (attempts included), possessing, transporting or selling elf (reg 22(7)(b) with Annexure 7; DFFE enforcement position, Sept 2025). Annexure 2 item 1 and DFFE brochure v23/1 rule (9) still print 1 September as the start date. See other_rules.

(2) Annexure 2 item 1 (Regulation 9, acts.co.za consolidation, never amended) reads 'from 1 September to 30

elf.review: Checked by an independent skeptic; 21 corrections applied
review_points: Miller's Point is the boundary of the Castle Rock restricted (no-take) zone of the TMNP MPA, which runs from Partridge Point to Millers Point. Telling anglers to fish 'Miller's Point' without naming that boundary can send them into a no-take zone. None of the cited Cape sources names Clovelly, Glenc

The Helderberg MPA bans all fishing between the Eerste River mouth (Macassar) and the Lourens River mouth (Strand), out to 500 m from the high-water mark, and Sealine has a 'Macassar beach fines' thread. Neither the habitat text nor the stand text warns of this. An angler walking east from Macassar

The cached thread supports the 4 pm, overcast, low-tide, calm-sea, rod-tip-low, slow-near-the-break retrieve. It says nothing about wading, and nothing places Roachy's Iron Candy fishing on the Muizenberg corner to Baileys stretch. The thread links Bailies Cottage to HIGH tide (surface lure or Iron

On the same Muizenberg/Sunrise stretch, Alan Lloyd says low tide is productive. Sean Mills (Strand/Gordon's Bay) gives the gullies at low tide and the beach at hi

These numbers are invented and are not flagged. Only the direction (white water helps daytime feeding) is sourced, from Mattheys. Calm water is not poor for elf in the sources: the main lure producer (Roachy) fishes 'calm seas', and the harbour-float and surface-lure tactics are tagged flat/small. f

The direction is sourced (Mattheys: dawn and dusk most active, ginger-beer-coloured water). The numbers are not, but they are missing from unverified while night and day_bright are listed. The unverified list is selective.

In the 2009 thread these are general remarks: Walt on harbour fishing ('Best times are from about October to April', then about cob) and Camo shorts on larger fish in general, in a thread mostly about kob and chokka. Only 'a lot of Elf at K/Bay over Easter' and the summer SE-wind remark tie to elf o

The thesis was not opened (abstract only), and 'whole adult stock' is stronger than an abstract can support. It also clashes with the profile's own evidence: elf are at the Cape in late September and caught in October and November (closed season), which are the same months given as spawn_months off
unverified: temp ideal_lo 16, ideal_hi 21 and max 24 are estimates. Only the 14 C minimum (US bluefish, Animal Diversity Web, not reopened by the reviewer) is sourced. The 8.4-27.5 C / 21.1 C FishBase figure is not on the cited summary page (it may be AquaMaps)
spawn month 9 is an estimate. Spawning off KZN is confirmed (Beckley & Connell 1996, abstract), and the Oct-Nov closed season exists to protect breeding
present month 5 (May) is an estimate; Cape sources give Oct/Dec to March/April
How much of the Cape stock migrates to KZN in winter is not established. Govender 1996 and Beckley & Connell 1996 were read as abstracts only, and the earlier wording 'whole adult stock' was dropped
trend weights (falling 0.8, steady 0.9, rising 0.75) have no source and are estimates
range weights are estimates: the spring-tide benefit comes from a Strand lure column about kob (Mattheys 2025), not elf
flow 0.7: estimate from elf preferring white water, rips and estuary mouths

tide weights are estimates. Pushing/high are partly backed (Baileys Cottage high-tide surface lure). Low was raised to 0.75 because Roachy's Iron Candy is fished at low tide and Muizenberg/Sunrise anglers report low tide as productive. Dropping 0.75 is a guess
sea weights are estimates. The direction is sourced (white water helps daytime feeding, Mattheys 2024; calm seas still produce on lures, Sealine 2013), but the magnitudes are not
light weights: the direction is sourced (dawn and dusk most active, Mattheys 2024) but every magnitude is an estimate. Night 0.35 and day_bright 0.35 have no source
clarity weights: the direction is sourced (ginger-beer-coloured water, Mattheys 2024), but the magnitudes are estimates
wind strength weights are estimates; only the link to the south-easter is sourced, not wind strength
big-one size of 3 to 5 kg for Cape shore fish is an estimate (10 kg blue elf and the 10.2 kg record are sourced)
surface lure size (12 to 15 cm, 20 to 30 g) and spoon weight band (18 to 28 g) are estimates within Mattheys' half-ounce to 2 oz range
fly tackle (7 to 8 wt, intermediate line, fly size 1 to 2/0, 40 lb bite tippet) is an estimate; the sources give only the fly pattern and colours
harbour float depth of 1 to 2 m and the float rig details are estimates. The float approach for elf rests on Jacita (May 2025), which the reviewer did not reopen

bait-rig sinker weights (1 to 2 oz, up to 3 oz in rough surf) are estimates

Several sources were not reopened by the reviewer: Animal Diversity Web, aquarium.co.za, Fish The Fly, Naysmith (Ski-Boat 2021), Jacita (May 2025), Mattheys (Oct 2023, Skitter lures) and Seaside Cottages
whether the closed season prohibits catch-and-release targeting or only retention was not checked against the current DFFE regulation text; the page treats elf as do-not-target in Oct-Nov

galjoen.name: Galjoen
galjoen.season_note: The legal season runs from 1 March to 14 October. The closed season runs from 15 October to the last day of February (MLRA regulations, Annexure 2; also the District Mail column and whalecoast.info). It covers the spawning period, when the fish move to deeper water to breed (FishBase; Britannica gives October to March). Galjoen stay on the coast all year and are sometimes hooked in summer (a Sealine Kogelbaai post records a closed-season catch). That is evidence they are present, not a reason to fish for them: in the closed season they may not be targeted, and any fish caught must be released. Winter is the classic Cape galjoen time. The Melkbos derby (Kommetjie lighthouse to Ysterfontein) is in late July, Jacita's June and July 2025 reports call it 'prime Galjoen time' from Cape Town to Hangklip, and one Sealine poster says they are 'plentiful in winter' and he no longer bothers fishing for them in summer. Fish are caught from the March opening onwards (Sealine Scarborough and Sea Point threads, March and April). The first half of October (1 to 14) is also legal. It is left out of present_months only because the engine works in whole months, so the engine should apply a date cut-off of 15 October if it can.

temp.basis: Estimate, partly backed. Cape anglers say cold, clear, still water is poor for galjoen (Sealine 'Galjoen' thread, Packkies, May 2008, open season). A February 2010 post says the same ('gallies at Gif don't seem to like cold water', jade fish), but it was made in the closed season about Gifkommetjie, which is inside the Cape of Good Hope no-take zone, so it is not used as a basis. Peak catches come in winter, when the Atlantic side is free of summer upwelling at roughly 12 to 15 C (also an estimate). FishBase/AquaMaps gives a modelled preferred range of 14.4 to 24.7 C (mean 16.7) for the whole species range from Angola to KwaZulu-Natal. Eggs in culture die below 14 to 16 C (van der Lingen 1991 UCT thesis), which is a spawning figure, not a feeding one. None of these numbers comes from a Cape-specific measurement.

galjoen.habitat: Shallow white-water gullies beside rocky reef, boulder beaches such as Bakoven (just north of the Karbonkelberg no-take zone, which starts at Oudekraal), kelp edges, and the sand-reef breaks and ledges next to them, such as the Strandfontein ledges, the Macassar ledges west of the Eerste River mouth, and Clovelly. The fish are often within a short cast, sometimes under 10 m from the shoreline: 'Short casts only' (Sealine), 'often found in rough surf right next to the shore' (SA History Online). Wikipedia gives shallow depths of around 10 m, often near the shore. They are strongly resident: of about 25,000 fish tagged at four reserve sites, roughly 95% stayed in one area. Fish over rock are almost black; fish over sand are silver-bronze.
galjoen.diet: Red bait (Pyura ascidians), small black mussels, barnacles, and red and coralline seaweed off rocky shores, plus white mussels (Donax) on sandy beaches. Anglers also catch them on bloodworm, wonder worm, coral worm and sand prawn.
galjoen.typical_size: Most shore fish are 30 to 40 cm (Macassar ledges 'mostly 30 to 35 cm', District Mail; fish of 41 and 44 cm reported, the 44 cm one tagged and released). Many shore fish are therefore at or under the 35 cm minimum. A big shore fish is 50 cm or more, about 3 to 4 kg. The species maximum is 80 cm TL and 6.5 kg (FishBase).
galjoen.handling: A recreational fishing permit is required. Minimum size is 35 cm TL, the bag limit is 2 per person per day, and the closed season runs from 15 October to the end of February. Do not target galjoen then, and release any fish caught. Many shore galjoen, including most Macassar ledge fish (30 to 35 cm), are under the 35 cm minimum. Measure every fish and release undersize ones in the water. Galjoen is a no-sale species (WWF-SASSI Red), listed as Near Threatened (NBA 2018), with the stock depleted to under 20% of optimal (SAAMBR). They grow slowly and live long. Release fish in the water or with wet hands or a wet cloth, back the hook out, and consider tag-and-release through the ORI tagging programme (District Mail, Mattheys 2023). No angling in the no-take zones. In the Table Mountain National Park MPA these are Karbonkelberg (Oudekraal to Hout Bay, including Llandudno and Sandy Bay), Cape of Good Hope (Scarborough to Hoek van die Bobbejaan, including Gifkommetjie and Olifantsbos), St James (St James to Kalk Bay tidal pools), Boulders, Castle Rock (Miller's Point to Partridge Point) and Paulsberg. Also off limits are the Helderberg MPA between the Eerste and Lourens river mouths (so fish the Macassar ledges only west of the Eerste mouth) and the Betty's Bay MPA restricted area. Red bait smell stays on the hands for days, so gloves help. Safety: rock anglers drown on this coast every year. Stay off the rocks in a rough sea, fish with a partner, and never turn your back on the sea. On the Strandfontein to Macassar stretch, fish in a group and in daylight, and check local angler-safety notices (Cape Argus reported an angler shot during a hijacking at Strandfontein in December 2025).

tactics.title: Pushing tide in the foamy gullies
tactics.lure_or_bait: Fresh white mussel, the Atlantic-side favourite, or red bait. Use a thumbnail-sized piece bound on with bait elastic. Wonder worm or bloodworm as a back-up.
tactics.rig: A 7 to 9 ft rod in a small sea, up to 10 ft in a moderate one, with 10 to 15 lb mono. A 1/0 short-shank hook (2/0 for a big bait), or a size 2 circle hook, on a short snood. A 1 to 2 oz sinker or an old spark plug in a small sea, 2 to 3 oz in a moderate one, on a lighter sinker link so it breaks free in the rocks. Bring plenty of spare sinkers and hooks.
tactics.retrieve: Lob it a short way into the foam and let the surge roll the bait along the gully floor. Keep the line just tight and lift into the fish when the knocks turn into a steady pull. Re-cast when the bait washes out or gets stripped.
tactics.depth: On the bottom of the gully, close in, often 10 to 20 m out (roughly 1 to 3 m deep, an estimate)
tactics.stand: On a ledge or boulder beach at the head of a gully where foamy water surges in and out, outside the no-take zones. Arrive at low tide to spot the gullies, then fish them as the tide pushes.
tactics.why: Captain Sparrow fishes from low to high tide so he can find the gullies 'while still lowish', looks for 'a nice gully with lots of foamy water moving in and out', and says 'Short casts only' (Sealine 76420, June 2013). baldrick also fishes close in with a 1/0 hook and spark plugs for sinkers (Sealine 5869).

tactics.title: Bigger winter sea: short casts into the white water
tactics.lure_or_bait: Fresh white mussel, or a white mussel and red bait combination, tied on firmly with bait elastic
tactics.rig: Up to a 10 ft rod, 12 to 15 lb mono, a 1/0 hook, and a 2 to 3 oz sinker or spark plug on a weak link. That is the top end of light tackle: if 3 oz will not hold, the sea is too big. Carry plenty of spares.
tactics.retrieve: Make a short cast to the inside edge of the white water, keep the rod up so the line stays off the rocks, and stay in touch. Bites often come as the backwash drains.
tactics.depth: Bottom, close in, where the reef meets sand (roughly 1 to 2 m, an estimate)
tactics.stand: A high, dry ledge well back from the reach of the sets, or the sand corner closest to a rock ledge, outside the no-take zones. If any wave washes over your rock, move to the beach corner or stop fishing. Never turn your back on the sea.
tactics.why: Galjoen 'don't mind it when the water is strong and churning and kicking up white water', and 'you can also fish for them in a bigger sea' (District Mail, 2023). On the Atlantic side a north-westerly that roughs up the Misty Cliffs side brings them on, but the same angler warns 'please be very careful here as the waves can get pretty hectic onto the rocks' (Captain Sparrow, Sealine 76420). baldrick moves up only to a 10 ft rod 'if the surf is a bit bigger' (Sealine 5869).

tactics.title: Rough sea: stay off the rocks
tactics.lure_or_bait: White mussel or red bait bound on with bait elastic
tactics.rig: A 10 ft rod, 12 to 15 lb mono, a 1/0 hook and a 3 oz sinker or spark plug on a weak link. That is the top end of light tackle: if 3 oz will not hold, do not fish.
tactics.retrieve: A short lob from the sand into the inside wash along the reef edge. Keep the line tight and lift on a steady pull.
tactics.depth: Bottom of the inside wash, close in
tactics.stand: Only on the sand of a beach corner next to reef, high above the reach of the biggest sets. Not on rocks, ledges or boulder beaches. If the wash reaches the back of the beach, or the only way to the water is over rock, do not fish today.
tactics.why: Galjoen tolerate churning water (District Mail, 2023), but the Cape angler who likes rough water also warns that 'the waves can get pretty hectic onto the rocks' (Sealine 76420), and rock anglers drown on this coast in big seas. This is a safety fallback, not a better day.

tactics.title: High tide on the sand-and-reef ledges
tactics.lure_or_bait: Sand prawn, bloodworm, or a 'mixed grill' of worm, prawn and mussel. Galjoen in False Bay take prawn and bloodworm well.
tactics.rig: A 7 to 10 ft rod and 12 to 15 lb mono. A 1/0 hook. A 1 to 2 oz ball or grapnel sinker on a weak link, up to 3 oz in a moderate sea if the lighter lead will not hold.
tactics.retrieve: Cast to the white water where the reef breaks onto sand and let it sit. Check the bait often, because sand crabs strip it.
tactics.depth: Bottom at the sand-reef break (roughly 1 to 3 m, an estimate)
tactics.stand: On the ledges and reef breaks of sand-and-reef shores, such as the Strandfontein and Swartklip ledges, the Macassar ledges west of the Eerste River mouth (east of it is the Helderberg no-take MPA), and the Clovelly corner of Fish Hoek beach. Fish the white water where the reef meets the sand. On the Strandfontein to Macassar stretch, fish in a group and in daylight.
tactics.why: Jacita reported Macassar and Broken Road 'fishing well, especially on high tide' for galjoen on bloodworm and mixed grill (May 2025). The Macassar ledges 'consistently produced galjoen throughout the season', and bigger seas helped (District Mail).

tactics.title: Flat and clear: light drift line into the deepest gully
tactics.lure_or_bait: A small piece of fresh white mussel, salted 'magic mussel', or a single worm
tactics.rig: A light 'flick stick' (8 to 9 ft) with 10 to 12 lb line. A size 1 to 1/0 hook. No sinker, or only a small running ball sinker, as a drift line.
tactics.retrieve: Flick it into the deepest gully or along the kelp edge and let the surge carry it naturally. Give the fish time to take it.
tactics.depth: Drifting down to the bottom of the deepest gully or along the kelp edge (roughly 2 to 4 m, an estimate)
tactics.stand: Above the deepest, darkest gully or a kelp hole, outside the no-take zones. Keep back from the edge and low against the skyline, because fish see you in clear water.
tactics.why: Clear, cold water with 'not much movement' is 'not good for gallie' (Packkies, Sealine 5869, May 2008), so these days rate low. If you do fish them, the local method for winter galjoen on the Fish Hoek side is 'a flick stick and drift line' (Enigma, Sealine 26561), and jade fish suggests salted 'magic mussel' (Sealine 34834, May 2010).

tactics.title: Churned-up water: smelly red bait close in
tactics.lure_or_bait: Aged ('rotten') red bait, or a white mussel and red bait combination, bound tight with bait elastic
tactics.rig: A 7 to 10 ft rod, 12 to 15 lb mono, a 1/0 short-shank hook (2/0 for a big bait), and a 1 to 2 oz sinker on a weak link, 2 to 3 oz if the surge keeps moving it.
tactics.retrieve: Make a short cast into the discoloured wash and leave the bait longer between checks. Re-cast if the surge drags it out of the gully.
tactics.depth: Bottom, close in (roughly 1 to 2 m, an estimate)
tactics.stand: At the nearest gully mouth where foamy, discoloured water is moving, outside the no-take zones. There is no need to cast past the first break.
tactics.why: Rotten red bait is the classic galjoen bait in Cape and Overberg bait tables (Village Voice, ShowMe). Galjoen 'go mad for red bait and white mussel' (Jacita), and red bait and mussel are the main baits in the District Mail column too.

tactics.title: Low tide: mark the gullies, fish the outer edge
tactics.lure_or_bait: White mussel or red bait
tactics.rig: A 7 to 9 ft rod, 10 to 15 lb mono, a 1/0 hook and a 1 to 2 oz sinker or spark plug on a weak link. Lighter lead is enough in the shallower water.
tactics.retrieve: Short casts into the deepest outer gully that still has water moving through it. Move back with the tide as it turns.
tactics.depth: Bottom of the outer gullies (roughly 1 to 2 m, an estimate)
tactics.stand: Only in a small sea: walk the exposed reef to note where the gullies and holes are, then fish the deepest outer gully from a safe, dry rock outside the no-take zones. Leave the outer reef before the push cuts you off.
tactics.why: Captain Sparrow fishes 'from low to high tide, so I can check for those gullies while still lowish' (Sealine 76420).

tactics.title: Red bait or white mussel in the nearest white water
tactics.lure_or_bait: Red bait or fresh white mussel bound on with elastic, with bloodworm or sand prawn as alternatives
tactics.rig: A 7 to 9 ft rod, up to 10 ft in a bigger sea, and 10 to 15 lb mono. A 1/0 short-shank hook (2/0 for a big bait). A 1 to 2 oz sinker or spark plug on a lighter sinker link, never more than 3 oz.
tactics.retrieve: Short cast into working white water next to rocks or reef, let the surge move the bait, keep the line tight, and lift when the pull is steady
tactics.depth: Bottom, close in
tactics.stand: Next to rocks or reef where white water is working, at the head of a gully, a boulder beach, or a sand-reef ledge, outside the no-take zones. If the sea is rough, stay off the rocks.
tactics.why: Galjoen feed in shallow white water next to rock and reef, mainly on red bait and mussels, and 'one can fish fairly light for these fish' (District Mail).

legal.bag_note: 2 per day in the open season (1 March to 14 October). Counts toward the aggregate of 10.

closed.rule: Catching is banned, not only keeping. Targeting galjoen counts as 'fishing' even with intent to release. Possession is also banned. Sources: reg 22(7)(b); reg 9 ('fishing, collecting, disturbing, keeping or controlling, or be in possession of'); brochure rule 13(d) ('shall not catch, disturb, land, keep or control').

legal.note: Reconciled: A and B agree. Annexure 7 (R.959) gives 'Closed season from 15 October to last day of February'. Annexure 2 item 2 (acts.co.za, cached) and brochure rule (10) give the same dates. The Act defines 'fishing' to include 'an attempt to undertake any such activity', so even catch-and-release targeting is banned in the closed season. A galjoen hooked by accident must be returned at once with
