leervis.review: Checked by an independent skeptic; 21 corrections applied
review_points: Wrong limit. The DFFE recreational table and the R1111 Annexure 7 list 'Mullets / harders, Family Mugilidae' with no minimum size and a daily bag limit of 50. Ten is the limit for pinky and strepie, the lines next to it in the table.

The Zandvlei Trust says catch and release of indigenous species is 'required by law', and Rietvlei says 'indigenous species must be returned'. A harder is indigenous, so you cannot keep one for bait at the very spots this tactic names. The 'dusk' window (an hour either side of sunset) also falls par
The quote is cut. Mattheys wrote 'especially deadly for the smaller fish in the estuaries'. Dropping 'smaller' overstates topwater for the 50-80 cm Zandvlei fish this tactic targets.

'Topwater Tigerfish Kings' (11 Apr 2023) is about tigerfish at Pongola and Lake Jozini in KZN. It says only that the Stella was developed for Zandvlei leervis feeding on round herring. Its line about putting 'in the time in low-light conditions to entice a surface eat' is about tigerfish, and it nev

The only leervis telemetry source actually opened says something different. Kilian, Murray et al. 2025 (AJMS 47(4), Breede Estuary, Western Cape) report that 'presence of L. amia was largely unaffected by month of the year', with the highest monthly residency index (0.33) in May. Fish stayed mostly

This contradicts the profile's own sources. Wale calls Zandvlei's population 'resident'. Breede telemetry (Western Cape) found adult presence 'largely unaffected by month'. The Zandvlei mouth is open all winter. The only Cape winter evidence is a June 2009 post saying the fish are 'less active', not

Zandvlei, the main leervis water, is closed to the sea all summer (the profile's peak months) apart from a few days each month. The Stella/tigerfish source (via search) says there is 'generally little to no tidal water movement'. Rush of Blue's receding-tide advice is generic SA estuary advice. With

'Dawn' and 'dusk' run an hour either side of sunrise and sunset, so about half of each window falls in Zandvlei's reported sunset-to-sunrise closure. Rietvlei fishing hours are 07:30-17:00, which in summer exclude dawn and dusk completely. The engine will rate and recommend fishing when it is report
unverified: Temperature cut-offs of 15/18/25/28 °C are estimates placed inside FishBase's modelled 16.2 to 29 °C range, which was not rechecked. No measured Cape thermal threshold was found.

Every condition weight (light, sea, tide, flow, range, trend, clarity, wind) is an estimate shaped by qualitative sources: first and last light best, likes a bit of chop, swell not too big, the dropping tide pushes bait off the banks, clear water better for fly. The spring/neap and pressure-trend weights have no source at all.

Tide and flow weights were flattened because Zandvlei, the main leervis water, is closed to the sea for most of summer. The engine should treat tide as neutral at Zandvlei while the mouth is closed, and apply the dropping-tide preference only at Milnerton Lagoon or an open Zandvlei mouth.

Night 0.25 is an estimate. Breede telemetry shows adults in the estuary overnight, but Zandvlei is reported closed to angling at night, and Rietvlei only allows fishing from 07:30 to 17:00. The engine should limit Zandvlei to sunrise to sunset (pending confirmation) and Rietvlei to 07:30 to 17:00.

present_months now covers all 12 months. Scoring May to September down through the cold-water temperature band is an estimate based on a June 2009 'less active' post. Peak months (December to April) are an estimate from Cape forum reports and generic Rush of Blue advice ('January to May' for the Southern and Eastern Cape).
The spawning migration to KwaZulu-Natal from September to November is general knowledge (Mann 2013 was not opened).

Leervis presence in the Muizenberg / Sunrise Beach surf: a 2008 Sealine poster had 'never heard of leeries caught in Muizenburg surf', so the surf tactic is a low-confidence bonus near the vlei mouth.
Current leervis presence at Milnerton Lagoon (thin, dated reports; ongoing pollution) and at Rietvlei (one 1980s 'Rietvlei Dam' report, which may refer to this Rietvlei).
Zandvlei angling closed from sunset to sunrise: from a 2012 FlyTalk post citing the 1974 Nature Conservation Ordinance, seen only in a cached search summary (the page itself returned 403).
The free dorsal and anal fin spines in the handling note come from general knowledge of the species, not from a source opened here.
Not checked in review: Botha's 'white is hard to beat', the 32.2 kg SA record, and the SASSI Red / no-sale status.
Stella fly size (6 to 9 cm), hook size (1/0) and the drop-ahead-of-the-swirl cast are estimates. The tying article gives only the hook model.
The Clouser tactic's day_bright trigger and the 5 to 10 sink count are estimates. The FlyTalk finding gives no time of day.
Surf rig beyond Mattheys's 7 ft / 4000 / 20 lb braid outfit (9 to 10 ft rod, 1.5 oz casting weight, 12 to 15 kg leader) is an estimate.
The coloured-water paddle-tail choice, the slow-and-deep cold-water tactic and the {downwind} bank preference are reasoned estimates, not quoted Cape advice.

maasbanker.name: Maasbanker
maasbanker.latin: Trachurus capensis (in older South African papers, Trachurus trachurus capensis)
maasbanker.season_note: Shore anglers catch maasbanker mostly in the deep harbours: Kalk Bay, Simon's Town and Gordon's Bay. In False Bay the run comes in spring and summer. A Kalk Bay regular reported 'tons of maasbanker' from about September (Sealine, 2009). In the same thread, other posters said Kalk Bay harbour fishes best from about October to April, and mainly in summer after the south-easter has been blowing. Those two remarks are about the harbour's fish in general, not maasbanker in particular. In mid-October 2010 none had been reported yet at Kalk Bay, so the start of the run in September or October varies. In January 2015 Kalk Bay was producing some maasbanker, and Simon's Town was reported second-hand. In February 2013 boat anglers anchored close to the Simon's Town harbour wall caught plenty. A November 2023 District Mail column sends anglers to the bigger harbours for them. The November to March peak is an estimate based on these few reports. An Angler Publications boat-fishing piece says harbours such as Simon's Town and Gordon's Bay hold small groups of baitfish most of the time, but it does not name maasbanker. present_months is set to all year, but June to August is an estimate: no winter catch was found, and Kalk Bay harbour in general is quieter outside October to April. Hout Bay harbour is plausible but unconfirmed for shore maasbanker. Further out, beyond the page's one-hour radius, Maasbaai near Hangklip is a known bait spot and was full of them in February 2015. Betty's Bay harbour was closed to fishing at last report (2016) and sits in the Betty's Bay MPA. The spawning stock sits on the Agulhas Bank east of 22 degrees E (Barange et al. 1998), far from Cape Town, so spawning has little effect on catches here. The fish caught from Cape harbours are mostly juveniles and sub-adults.

temp.basis: Estimate. When the FishBase summary page was fetched again on 2 Nov 2026, it gave only 'Subtropical; 14N - 37S' and no preferred temperature. The modelled (AquaMaps) range of about 9 to 15 C for the adult shelf stock that the researcher reported could not be found on the cited page. The inshore band is widened to cover summer harbour catches in False Bay, where the water is typically 16 to 21 C (estimate). The min of 9 C and max of 23 C are also estimates.

maasbanker.habitat: A pelagic shoaling fish of the continental shelf, found 0 to 500 m deep (usually 100 to 300 m), often over sand. The shoals stay close to the bottom by day and rise to feed in the surface waters at night (FishBase). Around Cape Town, shoals of juveniles and sub-adults come into deep, sheltered harbours: the Kalk Bay wall, the Simon's Town jetty just past the naval dockyard entrance, and Gordon's Bay harbour. Hout Bay harbour is plausible but unconfirmed. In harbours they hold along deep walls, around moored boats and in the harbour-mouth channel, and at night in water lit by quay or boat lights. Cape fly anglers also fish for them at night off the Strand Pavilion. They also hold off deep rocky points such as Maasbaai near Hangklip, but that is beyond the one-hour radius.
maasbanker.diet: Juveniles feed mainly on copepods. Adults eat small fish and a wide range of invertebrates (FishBase). In harbours they readily take slivers of sardine and chokka and small flashy flies. Their prey probably also includes euphausiids, mysids and larval squid (estimate).
maasbanker.typical_size: Shore-caught in Cape harbours: typically 15 to 25 cm (about 50 to 200 g), mostly immature fish. FishBase gives a common length of 30 cm FL, maturity at about 32.5 cm (range 20 to 33 cm) and a maximum of 60 cm FL. A big one from the shore is 35 to 45 cm (about 0.5 to 1 kg). The shore sizes are an estimate.
maasbanker.handling: Harmless (FishBase). However, a row of sharp bony scutes runs along the lateral line, and the small dorsal and anal spines can nick fingers. Sabiki strings carry about 6 hooks: unhook each fish before lowering again, and keep children clear when swinging fish in. Not protected; IUCN Least Concern (assessed 2017). You need a DFFE recreational angling permit. Check the current recreational bag limit before keeping fish for bait. To release a fish, unhook it over the water with wet hands and return it quickly, because they shed scales and tire fast. Keep only what you will use as bait or eat. Obey harbour-master no-fishing signs on working quays. No-take zones lie close to several spots: St James, just north of Kalk Bay; Boulders, just south of Simon's Town; Karbonkelberg (Oudekraal to Hout Bay), outside Hout Bay harbour; and the Helderberg MPA (Lourens River mouth west to the Eerste River mouth), next to Strand. Do not wander along the shore into any of them. Kalk Bay and Simon's Town are inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA. Its rules on chumming were not checked, so ask before using a chum bag. Betty's Bay harbour was closed to fishing at last report. Stay off the outer Kalk Bay wall, and any outer wall, when waves are washing over it.

tactics.title: Sabiki under the harbour lights after dark
tactics.lure_or_bait: Sabiki (bait-catcher) string of 6 small flash flies on size 10 hooks (8 to 12), each tipped with a thumbnail sliver of sardine or chokka; 20 to 30 g torpedo or bank sinker on the bottom snap
tactics.rig: Ready-made sabiki, 0.25 to 0.35 mm main line, light 2.1 to 2.7 m rod rated 2 to 6 kg, 2500 to 3000 spinning reel; sinker clipped to the bottom swivel
tactics.retrieve: Lower to where the light fades, then lift the rod tip 30 to 50 cm and let the string flutter back, with a 3 to 5 second pause. When one hooks, keep jigging gently for a few seconds so more load up, then wind up steadily
tactics.depth: Upper half of the water column, because the shoals rise to feed after dark. Start 2 to 4 m down and go shallower if fish show at the surface
tactics.stand: On the harbour wall or jetty where quay or boat lights shine on the water; work the line where light meets shadow. Kalk Bay: inside the main wall. Simon's Town: the jetty just past the naval dockyard entrance. Gordon's Bay: the harbour wall. Obey harbour no-fishing signs
tactics.colour: Pink or white flies, or luminous (glow) flies; plain silver flash works under bright lights
tactics.why: FishBase says the shoals rise to feed in the surface waters at night, and Sean Mills reports that night fishing at the Strand Pavilion targets maasbanker. Sabiki rigs are the standard harbour method (District Mail; Seaside Cottages for the Kalk Bay wall). Anglers often fish at night at Kalk Bay and the Simon's Town jetty (Seaside Cottages; Sealine 2015), but neither report says maasbanker bite at night. The night timing here rests on biology plus the Strand note (estimate)

tactics.title: Deep sabiki along the wall by day
tactics.lure_or_bait: Sabiki string with size 10 to 12 hooks, tipped with sardine skin; 30 to 40 g sinker
tactics.rig: Ready-made sabiki on 0.25 to 0.30 mm line, light 2.1 to 2.7 m rod rated 2 to 6 kg; sinker on the bottom snap
tactics.retrieve: Let it hit bottom and wind up 1 m, then make slow 20 to 40 cm lifts and drops. Work up the column in 1 m steps until you find them, then stay at that depth
tactics.depth: Bottom third, in the deepest water you can reach, because by day the shoals sit close to the bottom
tactics.stand: Deepest stretch of the harbour wall or the harbour-mouth channel (Kalk Bay, Simon's Town, Gordon's Bay), beside moored boats and in their shade where fishing is allowed
tactics.colour: Silver flash or natural colours; smaller flies (size 12) in bright, clear water
tactics.why: FishBase: shoals stay close to the bottom during the day. Angler Publications: harbours such as Gordon's Bay and Simon's Town hold small groups of baitfish (not named as maasbanker) most of the time, and sabiki jigs catch livebait there

tactics.title: Float-fished sardine sliver (chum only where allowed)
tactics.lure_or_bait: Sardine strip 2 to 3 cm, or a chokka sliver, on a size 10 to 8 fine-wire hook. Chum is optional: a frozen sardine block or chopped sardine in a mesh bag on a rope, used only where the rules allow it. Kalk Bay and Simon's Town are inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA, and its chumming rules were not checked, so ask first or fish the bait alone
tactics.rig: Small pencil or quill float (3 to 5 g), 1 to 3 m drop set with a stopper knot, 2 to 3 split shot, 50 cm trace of 0.25 to 0.30 mm fluorocarbon; ultralight 2 to 6 kg rod
tactics.retrieve: No retrieve: let it drift with the gentle current along the wall. Strike on a quick dip, because they snatch and spit
tactics.depth: 1 to 3 m below the surface at dusk and night; drop it deeper at dawn
tactics.stand: Inside the harbour (Kalk Bay, Simon's Town, Gordon's Bay), on the side where the gentle current carries the scent along the wall
tactics.why: The District Mail column sends anglers to the bigger harbours for maasbanker with sabiki rigs and an 'optional sardine block', but does not say how the block is used. The float version is an estimate: it suits calm water, where a float shows the quick bites

tactics.title: Micro-metal on ultralight spin
tactics.lure_or_bait: 5 to 15 g silver micro-jig, casting spoon or small Toby-type spoon; optionally a single sabiki fly as a teaser 50 cm above it
tactics.rig: Light 2 to 6 kg rod, 1000 to 2500 reel, PE 0.6 to 0.8 braid with 1 m of 4 to 6 kg fluorocarbon leader; swap the treble for a single size 4 to 6 hook
tactics.retrieve: Cast along the wall, count down 3 to 8 seconds, then retrieve quickly and steadily with sharp twitches; or rip-and-drop vertically under the wall
tactics.depth: Mid-water at dawn and dusk; just under the surface if the shoal is splashing
tactics.stand: End of the harbour wall or the harbour mouth, casting across the current line, or wherever terns or splashes show the shoal. Only in calm conditions, and never on an outer wall that waves wash over
tactics.colour: Silver or chrome; silver-green in bright light
tactics.why: Adults hunt small fish (FishBase), and fast flash suits a visual feeder in clear water at low light. No Cape source was found for this method (estimate)

tactics.title: Small baitfish fly at the edge of the lights
tactics.lure_or_bait: Size 6 to 8 Clouser minnow, flashy shrimp or epoxy minnow, 3 to 5 cm, in white, chartreuse or pink
tactics.rig: #5 to #7 weight rod, intermediate or sink-tip line, 2 to 3 m leader of 6 to 8 lb fluorocarbon
tactics.retrieve: Count it down to the shoal, then make short fast strips of 10 to 20 cm with brief pauses
tactics.depth: 1 to 3 m down, at the edge of the lit water
tactics.stand: Harbour wall or jetty above lit water (Kalk Bay, Simon's Town, Gordon's Bay), or the Strand Pavilion stretch at night, where Cape fly anglers target maasbanker. At Strand, fish only on the town beachfront east of the Lourens River mouth. The coast west of that mouth to the Eerste River is the no-take Helderberg MPA
tactics.colour: White or chartreuse with flash; pink under bright lights
tactics.why: Sean Mills' 'Saltwater fly fishing in the W/Cape' says night fishing at the Strand Pavilion targets maasbanker. FishBase says the shoals feed near the surface at night

tactics.title: Strong wind: vertical in the lee of the wall
tactics.lure_or_bait: Sabiki cut down to 3 or 4 flies on size 10 hooks, sardine-tipped, with a 40 to 60 g sinker
tactics.rig: Shortened sabiki on 0.30 mm line, 2.1 to 2.7 m light rod rated 2 to 6 kg with a stiffer tip so you can feel bites in the wind
tactics.retrieve: Drop straight down beside the wall with short lifts, keeping the line vertical so the wind cannot belly it
tactics.depth: Near the bottom up to mid-water
tactics.stand: The sheltered side of the harbour wall or the inner basin, out of the wind. Never fish an outer wall or rocks when waves wash over them, and stay home if the sea is rough
tactics.why: Estimate. Boat anglers anchored by the Simon's Town harbour wall caught plenty in a howling wind (Sealine, Feb 2013); the shore equivalent is unconfirmed. Fishing vertically in the lee of the wall keeps the line out of the wind

tactics.title: Coloured water: glow flies and scent
tactics.lure_or_bait: Sabiki with luminous (glow) or chartreuse flies, every hook tipped with sardine
tactics.rig: Sabiki on 0.25 to 0.30 mm line with a 30 to 40 g sinker, light 2 to 6 kg rod
tactics.retrieve: Slow lifts with long pauses (5 to 10 seconds) so the scent does the work
tactics.depth: Bottom half of the water column
tactics.stand: The most sheltered inner corner of the harbour, where the water stays cleanest and calmest
tactics.why: Sardine-tipped sabikis are the standard harbour method (District Mail). It is an estimate that glow flies and scent make up for poor visibility. A chum bag would add scent, but check the TMNP MPA rules on chumming at Kalk Bay and Simon's Town first (not checked)

tactics.title: Sabiki worked through the water column off the harbour wall
tactics.lure_or_bait: Sabiki (bait-catcher) string, size 10 hooks tipped with sardine or chokka slivers, 20 to 40 g sinker
tactics.rig: Ready-made sabiki on light 2 to 6 kg spinning tackle, 0.25 to 0.35 mm line
tactics.retrieve: Drop to the bottom, then lift and drop slowly, working up the column a metre at a time until you find the shoal; stay at that depth
tactics.depth: Search the whole column: near the bottom by day, upper water after dark
tactics.stand: Deep harbour walls and jetties: Kalk Bay wall, Simon's Town jetty, Gordon's Bay harbour. Hout Bay harbour is plausible but unconfirmed for shore maasbanker
tactics.colour: Pink, white or silver flash; glow at night
tactics.why: Sabiki rigs are the standard Cape way to catch maasbanker in the bigger harbours (District Mail; Seaside Cottages for Kalk Bay, Simon's Town and Gordon's Bay; Angler Publications on sabiki for harbour baitfish)

legal.bag_note: No bag limit. Excluded from the aggregate of 10 (reg 22(7)(f)).
legal.note: A and B agree and both match R.959. No closed season.
legal.quote: Horse mackerel / maasbanker | Trachurus trachurus capensis | none | none

maasbanker.review: Checked by an independent skeptic; 18 corrections applied
review_points: The only cached source on that spot (Sealine Kleinmond thread, 2016) says the Bettiesbay Harbour/Whaling Station breakwater is closed to fishing ('Should it ever open for fishing again'). It sits at Stony Point, in the Betty's Bay MPA. The profile sends anglers there with no warning, and it is also

The 2011 source is a newcomer listing catches across Kalk Bay, Hermanus and Hout Bay. It does not say harbour or shore, and the gurnard in that list points to boat fishing. The only Hout Bay harbour thread in the cache never mentions maasbanker. No source says which Hout Bay quays allow fishing or a

The Simon's Town report is from a boat ('we anchored very close to the harbor wall', fish released 'next to the boat'), so it is not shore evidence. The Kalk Bay quote describes the seasonal pattern for the harbour's fish in general, not fishing during a strong wind and not maasbanker. Nothing suppo

This merges separate posts. 'Tons of maasbanker' from September is maasbanker-specific. 'Best times are from about October to April' (Walt) and 'only really produces fish during the summer months when the SE wind has been blowing' (Dorado75) are general statements about Kalk Bay harbour, not about m
